| Module components  | Descriptions  | Who is responsible for prep? | Appr. weekly workload for the learner | Weight in the assessment  |
| Weekly digital content  | \*Provides self-paced learning opportunities.  \*Can be studied before or after the workshop by the participants. \*Should be connected with the module learning outcomes, the workshop and the weekly assignment.  \*Offers learning resources for different levels of learning. e.g intro material and some more advanced for experienced participants.  \*Comes from Coursera + facilitator's curated content.  \*Both video and reading for variety. \*Should be ready before the week opens. Gets published on Mondays. | Module facilitator | 4 hours | N/A |
| Weekly assignment  | \*Provides further practice and application of the previously learned material.  \*Should not be checking for knowledge / remembering. Aims at higher level & more complex thinking and putting things into real life scenarios.  \*There is a variety in the format & method. Check this page for guidance.  \*Could be individually submitted or group work.  \*Use of discussions on Canvas is an option.  | Module facilitator  | 8 hours  | 30% |
| Evaluation rubric for the assignment  | \* Aims to create transparency and objectivity in the assignment's evaluation \* Contains the module's learning outcomes See an example here  | Module facilitator | N/A | N/A |
| Weekly workshop | \*Allows for deeper understanding of the module content.  \*There is a balance between lecture and active participation. \* There is a lot of room for real-life examples from business + discussions. \* Follows the 4MAT structure. | Module facilitator | 90 min | N/A |
| Module project  | \*Assigned in the last week of the module.  \*More comprehensive than weekly assignments \*Allows for culmination of the learning in the whole module \*Could involve group work, their own business context, presentations etc. | Module facilitator | 10 hours  | 50% |
| Knowledge checks  | \* To reinforce their understanding and retention of the weekly material \* The module facilitator provides a key content, the programme manager creates 10 quiz questions with the assistance of AI tools. \* Accessed on Canvas and automatically graded.  | Module facilitator & prg. management | 10-20 min | 10% |
| Action Learning Reflective Account | \* It is for reflecting after each action learning session facilitated by the action learning coach. \* They are evaluated by the action learning coach \* (might be less frequent) | AL coach | 1 hour  | 10% |
| Mentoring  | \* A weekly group session for the participants' questions.  | Mentor | 1 hour  | N/A |

| Assignment Template: \[Assignment Title\] |
|  |
| Objective/Focus: Provide a brief statement outlining the motivation behind the assignment. This sets the context and purpose for students. |
|  |
| Learning Outcome: Specify the learning outcome(s) associated with the assignment - they are in the Modules-competencies-learning outcomes sheet. Please bear in mind that every week is a different learning outcome and at the end of the module, all the learning outcomes were measured.  |
|  |
| Instructions: |
|  |
| Introduction: |
| Briefly introduce the assignment topic and its relevance. |
| State the objective of the assignment |
| Task Description: |
| Clearly outline the tasks or questions that students need to address. |
| Break down the assignment into manageable sections if applicable. |
| Required Resources: |
| List any essential resources, materials, or references that students should consult - can be a resource from the weekly resources or any other. |
| Guidelines: |
| Provide any specific guidelines, formatting requirements, or limitations. |
| Clarify expectations |
| Submission Instructions: |
| Specify the submission format |

|  |
| Introduction to Blockchain: Understanding the underlying principles and decentralized nature |
| Exploring Blockchain Networks: Public, private, and consortium blockchains |
| Smart Contracts: Applications and benefits in business processes |

|  |

|  |
| Introduction to Cryptocurrencies: Bitcoin, Ethereum, and beyond |
| Cryptocurrency Mining: How it works and its environmental considerations |
| Cryptocurrency Exchanges and Wallets: Trading, storing, and securing digital assets |
| Regulatory Landscape and Challenges: Navigating the evolving legal and regulatory framework |
|  |

|  |
| NFTs (Non-Fungible Tokens) Demystified: Understanding unique digital assets |
| NFTs in Art and Entertainment: Revolutionizing creative industries |
| Tokenizing Real-World Assets: The concept of tokenization and its potential applications |
| Investing in NFTs: Risks, opportunities, and best practices for business professionals |
|  |
| Week 4: Blockchain Strategy and Future Outlook |
|  |
| Integrating Blockchain into Business Models: Identifying opportunities and challenges |
| Blockchain Implementation: Strategies for successful adoption and scalability |
| Decentralized Finance (DeFi) and its Impact: Exploring the disruption of traditional finance |
| The Future of Blockchain Technology: Emerging trends and possibilities |

| MODULE 1:  | DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module provides participants with a comprehensive understanding of the drivers, challenges, and strategies associated with navigating the rapidly evolving digital landscape. The module explores the transformative power of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving organizational change. Students will delve into the competitive positioning and future-proofing strategies necessary for success in an era of exponential growth and disruptive innovation. The module also covers the building blocks of a digital organization, emphasizing the importance of creating an agile and adaptable framework. Additionally, students will be introduced to emerging technologies and developments, using frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies shaping the digital landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Digital transformation and strategies   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Demonstrate a deep understanding of the drivers behind digital transformation to formulate well-structured strategies  \- Effectively assess the role of technology as a disruptor and enabler of change within various business contexts  \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| M1 Week 1 content  | Reading: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/rewired-mckinsey-guide-outcompeting-age-digital-ai-wagner-freitas/  rewired-mckinsey-guide-outcompeting-age-digital-ai  Coursera: https://www.coursera.org/learn/introduction-to-digital-transformation-part-1 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 1 Workshop Outline  | \[merged\] Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers  Duration: 1.5 hours   Part 1: Why - The Urgency of Digital Transformation (15 minutes)  Opening Remarks (2 minutes)  Briefly introduce the topic and the significance of understanding digital transformation in today's business landscape.  Mini-Lecture: The Shift in Business Landscape (5 minutes)  Discuss how technology is disrupting traditional markets and creating new ones.  Group Discussion: Impacts of Being Left Behind (8 minutes)  Participants share examples of companies that failed to adapt and the consequences they faced.    Part 2: What - Understanding the Drivers of Digital Transformation (25 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Key Drivers Explained (10 minutes)  Explore elements like customer expectations, competition, and technological advancements as drivers.  Breakout Groups: Industry-Specific Drivers (10 minutes)  Participants are divided into groups to identify and discuss key drivers in their respective industries.  Group Sharing (5 minutes)  Each group presents their findings.    Part 3: How - Enabling Digital Transformation (30 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Role of Leadership, Culture, and Technology (10 minutes)  Discuss how companies can strategically leverage various internal and external factors for successful transformation.  Case Study Analysis: Digital Transformation Success Story (10 minutes)  Participants review a real-world example of a company that successfully underwent digital transformation.  Group Exercise: Plan a Simple Digital Transformation Strategy (10 minutes)  Groups work on drafting a rudimentary digital strategy for a hypothetical or real business.    Part 4: What If - Future-Proofing and Challenges (15 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Potential Risks and Barriers (5 minutes)  Discuss potential challenges like resistance to change, technological constraints, and budget limitations.  Group Discussion: Contingency Plans (8 minutes)  Participants discuss how to future-proof digital strategies and develop contingency plans.  Closing Remarks (2 minutes)  Summarize the key takeaways and preview the topics for the next session. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Part 2: What - Understanding the Drivers of Digital Transformation (25 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Key Drivers Explained (10 minutes)  Explore elements like customer expectations, competition, and technological advancements as drivers.  Breakout Groups: Industry-Specific Drivers (10 minutes)  Participants are divided into groups to identify and discuss key drivers in their respective industries.  Group Sharing (5 minutes)  Each group presents their findings.    Part 3: How - Enabling Digital Transformation (30 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Role of Leadership, Culture, and Technology (10 minutes)  Discuss how companies can strategically leverage various internal and external factors for successful transformation.  Case Study Analysis: Digital Transformation Success Story (10 minutes)  Participants review a real-world example of a company that successfully underwent digital transformation.  Group Exercise: Plan a Simple Digital Transformation Strategy (10 minutes)  Groups work on drafting a rudimentary digital strategy for a hypothetical or real business.    Part 4: What If - Future-Proofing and Challenges (15 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Potential Risks and Barriers (5 minutes)  Discuss potential challenges like resistance to change, technological constraints, and budget limitations.  Group Discussion: Contingency Plans (8 minutes)  Participants discuss how to future-proof digital strategies and develop contingency plans.  Closing Remarks (2 minutes)  Summarize the key takeaways and preview the topics for the next session. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Group Discussion: Impacts of Being Left Behind (8 minutes)  Participants share examples of companies that failed to adapt and the consequences they faced.    Part 2: What - Understanding the Drivers of Digital Transformation (25 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Key Drivers Explained (10 minutes)  Explore elements like customer expectations, competition, and technological advancements as drivers.  Breakout Groups: Industry-Specific Drivers (10 minutes)  Participants are divided into groups to identify and discuss key drivers in their respective industries.  Group Sharing (5 minutes)  Each group presents their findings.    Part 3: How - Enabling Digital Transformation (30 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Role of Leadership, Culture, and Technology (10 minutes)  Discuss how companies can strategically leverage various internal and external factors for successful transformation.  Case Study Analysis: Digital Transformation Success Story (10 minutes)  Participants review a real-world example of a company that successfully underwent digital transformation.  Group Exercise: Plan a Simple Digital Transformation Strategy (10 minutes)  Groups work on drafting a rudimentary digital strategy for a hypothetical or real business.    Part 4: What If - Future-Proofing and Challenges (15 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Potential Risks and Barriers (5 minutes)  Discuss potential challenges like resistance to change, technological constraints, and budget limitations.  Group Discussion: Contingency Plans (8 minutes)  Participants discuss how to future-proof digital strategies and develop contingency plans.  Closing Remarks (2 minutes)  Summarize the key takeaways and preview the topics for the next session. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1 Assignment  | Weekly Assignment: Analysing the Drivers behind Digital Transformation Select one specific industry or organization that has undergone a significant digital transformation. It could be a company you're familiar with or one you discover through your research.  Digital Transformation Drivers: Discuss at least three key drivers that are influencing digital transformation in your chosen subject. Impact: Discuss the impact of digital transformation on the industry or organization. How has it changed their operations, customer experiences, or business models? Reflection: Conclude your assignment with a brief reflection on what you've learned from this analysis. How can this understanding of digital transformation drivers be applied to your role or industry? Word limit: 250 words  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Learning Outcome: Demonstrate an understanding of the key drivers behind digital transformation in formulating well-structured strategies for a chosen industry or organization.  Evaluation Criteria:  Analysis of Digital Transformation Drivers 5 (Excellent): Thoroughly discusses at least three key drivers with exceptional clarity and insight. Demonstrates an exceptional understanding of how these drivers are influencing digital transformation in the chosen subject. Provides insightful examples and evidence to support the analysis. 4 (Very Good): Discusses at least three key drivers in a clear and concise manner. Shows a strong understanding of how these drivers influence digital transformation. Provides relevant examples and evidence to support the analysis. 3 (Satisfactory): Discusses three key drivers but may lack some depth in analysis. Demonstrates a satisfactory understanding of how these drivers influence digital transformation. Provides some examples and evidence. 2 (Fair): Discusses fewer than three key drivers, and the analysis is limited. Shows a basic understanding of digital transformation drivers but lacks depth. Provides minimal examples or evidence. 1 (Poor): Fails to discuss digital transformation drivers effectively or provides inaccurate information. Demonstrates a lack of understanding of the key drivers. Lacks examples and evidence. Analysis of Impact 5 (Excellent): Provides a comprehensive and insightful analysis of the impact of digital transformation on the industry or organization. Clearly identifies and explains how it has transformed operations, customer experiences, and business models. Supported by compelling examples and evidence. 4 (Very Good): Offers a clear analysis of the impact of digital transformation. Identifies and explains how it has transformed operations, customer experiences, and business models. Provides relevant examples and evidence. 3 (Satisfactory): Presents a reasonable analysis of the impact of digital transformation. Discusses changes in operations, customer experiences, and business models, but may lack some depth. Offers some examples and evidence. 2 (Fair): Provides limited analysis of the impact of digital transformation. Discusses changes superficially and with minimal depth. Offers few examples or evidence. 1 (Poor): Fails to analyze the impact of digital transformation effectively or provides inaccurate information. Demonstrates a lack of understanding of the impact. Lacks examples and evidence. Reflection on Learning 5 (Excellent): Offers a thoughtful and insightful reflection on the assignment, demonstrating a deep understanding of the subject matter. Clearly articulates how the learning from this analysis can be applied to their role or industry with innovative and well-supported ideas. 4 (Very Good): Provides a clear reflection on the assignment, indicating a good understanding of the subject matter. Articulates how the learning can be applied to their role or industry with relevant ideas and examples. 3 (Satisfactory): Offers a basic reflection on the assignment, demonstrating a reasonable understanding of the subject matter. Indicates how the learning can be applied to their role or industry with some relevant ideas. 2 (Fair): Provides a limited reflection with minimal depth. Offers basic ideas about the application of learning to their role or industry but lacks detail or relevance. 1 (Poor): Fails to provide a meaningful reflection or application of learning. Demonstrates a lack of understanding or relevance in applying the knowledge.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 1:  | DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module provides participants with a comprehensive understanding of the drivers, challenges, and strategies associated with navigating the rapidly evolving digital landscape. The module explores the transformative power of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving organizational change. Students will delve into the competitive positioning and future-proofing strategies necessary for success in an era of exponential growth and disruptive innovation. The module also covers the building blocks of a digital organization, emphasizing the importance of creating an agile and adaptable framework. Additionally, students will be introduced to emerging technologies and developments, using frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies shaping the digital landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Digital transformation and strategies   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 learning outcome | Effectively assess the role of technology as a disruptor and enabler of change within various business contexts   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 1 Week 2 Content  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 2 Workshop Outline  | \[merged\] Workshop Outline: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler  Duration: 1.5 hours    Part 1: Why - The Dual Role of Technology (15 minutes)  Opening Remarks (2 minutes)  Introduction to the paradoxical role technology plays in modern business.  Mini-Lecture: Technology as a Disruptor (5 minutes)  Discuss how emerging technologies can unsettle established industries.  Group Discussion: Real-World Agitations (8 minutes)  Participants share instances where technology has disrupted traditional business models.    Part 2: What - Identifying the Agitating and Enabling Technologies (25 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Overview of Agitating Technologies (10 minutes)  Introduce technologies like AI, blockchain, and IoT as forces that shake up business norms.  Breakout Groups: Exploring Enabling Technologies (10 minutes)  Participants are divided into groups to discuss technologies that have enabled businesses to adapt or evolve.  Group Sharing (5 minutes)  Each group shares their insights about how different technologies act as enablers.    Part 3: How - Strategic Approaches to Technology (30 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Technology Assessment Frameworks (10 minutes)  Introduce frameworks for evaluating the risks and rewards of adopting new technologies.  Case Study: Leveraging Technology for Competitive Advantage (10 minutes)  Analyze a real-world example where a company successfully used technology as an enabler.  Group Exercise: Creating a Technology Strategy Plan (10 minutes)  Groups develop a simplified technology strategy for a hypothetical or existing business.    Part 4: What If - Risks and Ethical Considerations (15 minutes)  Mini-Lecture: Risk Mitigation and Ethics (5 minutes)  Discuss the ethical implications and risks, such as data privacy and security concerns.  Group Discussion: Scenario Planning (8 minutes)  Participants talk about various "what if" scenarios where technology could either enable or disrupt their business models.  Closing Remarks (2 minutes)  Summarize key takeaways and set the stage for the next workshop topic.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 2 Assignment  (Graded Discussion) | (Will be a discussion activity this time) Analyzing Technology's Role as an Agitator and Enabler in an Organization  In this discussion activity, we would like you to look around and pick a use case again as in the previous assignment. It always helps to analyze the existing practices to understand the nature of the fast-paced transformation and to learn from them. Now select a company that you believe has experienced technology as either an agitator, an enabler, or both. Again, this could be your own company. Introduce the company and its industry context. What specific technology or technologies have acted as an agitator or enabler? Provide a brief description.  Role as an Agitator:  If the technology has disrupted the company's traditional business model, explain how.  What were the challenges and consequences faced?  Role as an Enabler:  If the technology has enabled the company to gain a competitive edge, achieve efficiencies, or open new markets, explain how.  What were the benefits and outcomes?  Challenge each other: Read through at least one peer's response in this discussion and reply them. What insightful question would you ask your peer about their chosen organization and its technology-driven changes to encourage them to broaden their perspective or delve deeper into their analysis. Keep the discussion going\!   Word Limit: 250 words |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  |  only 1 criteria for this one:  Analysis of Technological Impact (Agitator or Enabler):  Excellent (5): Provides a comprehensive analysis identifying specific technologies that have significantly agitated or enabled change in the chosen company. Offers detailed and clear descriptions supported by strong evidence. Excellent demonstration of critical thinking in the analysis.  Very Good (4): Offers a good analysis of the technologies involved as either agitator or enabler, but lacks some depth or clarity in explanations. Satisfactory (3): Provides a basic analysis of the technologies' roles, but lacks depth, clarity, or evidence to support claims. Fair (2): Limited analysis provided; lacks clarity or specificity in identifying technologies and their roles as agitator or enabler. Poor (1): Fails to analyze or identify specific technologies and their roles as agitator or enabler in the chosen company. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| The prompt for the evaluation criteria:  | As a learning designer, you are going to create an evaluation rubric for an assignment. Using target the learning outcome , create 3-4 evaluation criteria associated with it. Then, create ratings from 5-1 with descriptions for each rating. 5: Excellent, 4: Very Good, 3: Satisfactory, 2: Fair, 1: Poor. The learning outcome/objective: Effectively assess the role of technology as an enabler or agitator of change within various business contexts. Here is the assignment: In this discussion activity, we would like you to look around and pick a use case again as in the previous assignment. It always helps to analyze the existing practices to understand the nature of the fast-paced transformation and to learn from them. Now select a company that you believe has experienced technology as either an agitator, an enabler, or both. Again, this could be your own company. Introduce the company and its industry context. What specific technology or technologies have acted as an agitator or enabler? Provide a brief description. Role as an Enabler:  If the technology has enabled the company to gain a competitive edge, achieve efficiencies, or open new markets, explain how.  What were the benefits and outcomes? | MODULE 1:  | DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module provides participants with a comprehensive understanding of the drivers, challenges, and strategies associated with navigating the rapidly evolving digital landscape. The module explores the transformative power of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving organizational change. Students will delve into the competitive positioning and future-proofing strategies necessary for success in an era of exponential growth and disruptive innovation. The module also covers the building blocks of a digital organization, emphasizing the importance of creating an agile and adaptable framework. Additionally, students will be introduced to emerging technologies and developments, using frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies shaping the digital landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Digital transformation and strategies   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Demonstrate a deep understanding of the drivers behind digital transformation to formulate well-structured strategies  \- Effectively assess the role of technology as a disruptor and enabler of change within various business contexts  \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 1 Week 3 Content  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 3 Workshop Outline | Workshop Outline: Building Blocks of Digital Organizations  Duration: 1.5 hours  Why (15 minutes)  Objective: To impress upon students the importance of building blocks in achieving organizational objectives and adhering to ethical considerations in digital transformation.  Activity 1: Introduction to the "Why" using a real-world case study, such as how Amazon has used cloud computing, data analytics, and AI to transform retail. Point out how these building blocks align with Amazon's strategic objectives and ethical considerations like customer privacy.  What (30 minutes)  Objective: To introduce the key building blocks that form the foundation of digital organizations.  Activity 1: Mini-lecture listing and explaining these key building blocks such as Cloud Computing, Data Analytics, AI, Cybersecurity, IoT, and Agile Methodologies.  Activity 2: Quick quizzes or polls after each building block to test understanding and retention.  How (30 minutes)  Objective: To equip students with the skills to develop digital transformation strategies using these building blocks, aligned with organizational objectives and ethics.  Activity 1: Breakout sessions where groups select an organizational scenario, identify relevant building blocks, and craft a mini digital transformation strategy keeping in mind organizational objectives and ethics.  Activity 2: Groups present their strategies and receive feedback from peers and the instructor.  What if (15 minutes)  Objective: To encourage foresight into how the building blocks might evolve and how strategies need to adapt.  Activity 1: Facilitated class discussion hypothesizing future developments in building blocks like AI ethics, quantum computing, or decentralized technologies.  Activity 2: Summarize key takeaways and how they can be applied to the students' own organizations or hypothetical business scenarios. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 3 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment  | Assignment: Toward an Effective Technology Operating Model    Within the framework of Technology Operating Model (TOM) presented by Deloitte, there are some dimensions that the organisations need to make choices for. Now go back to the article:  Deloitte-Volume 2 \_ The 9 big shifts to the Technology Operating Model (Canvas link here). Read through page 8 on the 15 dimensions, and consider these dimensions within the context of your company. Then select 3 out of 15 dimensions that you think are most critical for your company, and answer the questions in that dimension in a detailed way. Explain why your company made these specific choices. If your company has not gone through any of these, then you may make an argument as to how it should handle each dimension.   Word limit: 250 words   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 1:  | DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module provides participants with a comprehensive understanding of the drivers, challenges, and strategies associated with navigating the rapidly evolving digital landscape. The module explores the transformative power of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving organizational change. Students will delve into the competitive positioning and future-proofing strategies necessary for success in an era of exponential growth and disruptive innovation. The module also covers the building blocks of a digital organization, emphasizing the importance of creating an agile and adaptable framework. Additionally, students will be introduced to emerging technologies and developments, using frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies shaping the digital landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Digital transformation and strategies   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Demonstrate a deep understanding of the drivers behind digital transformation to formulate well-structured strategies  \- Effectively assess the role of technology as a disruptor and enabler of change within various business contexts  \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 1 Week 4 Content  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 4 Workshop Outline | Workshop Outline: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Business Strategies  Duration: 1.5 hours  Why (15 minutes)  Objective: To establish the critical role of competitive positioning and future-proofing in sustaining business growth.  Activity 1: Brief discussion using the examples of Tesla and Yahoo to illustrate the impact of good and bad competitive positioning.  Activity 2: Quick audience poll asking what elements they consider crucial for sustaining long-term business growth.  What (30 minutes)  Objective: To introduce the key components required to develop a sound competitive positioning strategy and a future-proof business plan.  Activity: Mini-lecture covering the principles of competitive positioning, such as Unique Selling Proposition (USP), target audience, and differentiation. Explanation of what future-proofing means in the context of business strategy, emphasizing adaptability and resilience.  How (30 minutes)  Objective: To guide students in developing their own competitive positioning and future-proof business strategies.  Activity 1: Breakout sessions where students work on creating a SWOT analysis and Porter's Five Forces model for a given or chosen company.  Activity 2: Groups reconvene to present their analyses and strategies, followed by peer review and feedback.  What If (15 minutes)  Objective: To challenge students to consider scenarios that could test the resilience of their business strategies.  Activity: Facilitated discussion on what contingencies should be in place to adapt to disruptive technologies, regulatory changes, or shifts in consumer behavior. | \[merged\] Week 4 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Assignment  | Assignment: Crafting Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Business Strategies  Objective: To develop and articulate a competitive positioning and future-proof business strategy for a chosen or assigned company.  Instructions:  Company Selection: Choose a real-life company or use a hypothetical business in an industry you are familiar with.  SWOT Analysis: Perform a brief SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis on the selected company.  Competitive Positioning: Based on your SWOT analysis, articulate the company's Unique Selling Proposition (USP), identify the target audience, and list the key differentiators that give it a competitive edge.  Future-Proof Strategy: Propose three initiatives the company can undertake to future-proof its business model. These could involve technological innovation, market diversification, or organizational changes.  Contingency Plans: Outline a basic 'What If' scenario analysis for one of the future-proofing initiatives. What would the company do if the initiative didn't go as planned?  Submission Format: Submit a 2-3 page PDF document containing the above elements. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 2:  | Data-Driven Organisations   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In this module, you will have a journey into the core of modern organisations, where data stands as a cornerstone for informed decision-making. Focusing on the critical competency of data leadership and strategic data utilisation, you will recognize the paramount role of data leadership in today's business landscape, and delve into the principles of data management and governance, enabling effective and ethical data utilisation. Building on this knowledge, you will discuss the data-driven strategies that serve as the driving force behind business growth and innovation. Moreover, you will learn to effectively communicate the value of data literacy, fostering a culture of data-driven decision-making within organisations. As you progress through this module, you will embrace the role of data leadership, ensuring a sustainable and innovative future for your organisation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Data leadership and strategic utilisation of data |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the significance of data leadership in contemporary organisations \- Analyse the key principles of data management and governance for effective utilisation of data \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| week assignments build up to end-project |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 2:  | Data-Driven Organisations   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In this module, you will have a journey into the core of modern organisations, where data stands as a cornerstone for informed decision-making. Focusing on the critical competency of data leadership and strategic data utilisation, you will recognize the paramount role of data leadership in today's business landscape, and delve into the principles of data management and governance, enabling effective and ethical data utilisation. Building on this knowledge, you will discuss the data-driven strategies that serve as the driving force behind business growth and innovation. Moreover, you will learn to effectively communicate the value of data literacy, fostering a culture of data-driven decision-making within organisations. As you progress through this module, you will embrace the role of data leadership, ensuring a sustainable and innovative future for your organisation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Data leadership and strategic utilisation of data |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the significance of data leadership in contemporary organisations \- Analyse the key principles of data management and governance for effective utilisation of data \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 2:  | Data-Driven Organisations   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In this module, you will have a journey into the core of modern organisations, where data stands as a cornerstone for informed decision-making. Focusing on the critical competency of data leadership and strategic data utilisation, you will recognize the paramount role of data leadership in today's business landscape, and delve into the principles of data management and governance, enabling effective and ethical data utilisation. Building on this knowledge, you will discuss the data-driven strategies that serve as the driving force behind business growth and innovation. Moreover, you will learn to effectively communicate the value of data literacy, fostering a culture of data-driven decision-making within organisations. As you progress through this module, you will embrace the role of data leadership, ensuring a sustainable and innovative future for your organisation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Data leadership and strategic utilisation of data |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the significance of data leadership in contemporary organisations \- Analyse the key principles of data management and governance for effective utilisation of data \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 2:  | Data-Driven Organisations   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In this module, you will have a journey into the core of modern organisations, where data stands as a cornerstone for informed decision-making. Focusing on the critical competency of data leadership and strategic data utilisation, you will recognize the paramount role of data leadership in today's business landscape, and delve into the principles of data management and governance, enabling effective and ethical data utilisation. Building on this knowledge, you will discuss the data-driven strategies that serve as the driving force behind business growth and innovation. Moreover, you will learn to effectively communicate the value of data literacy, fostering a culture of data-driven decision-making within organisations. As you progress through this module, you will embrace the role of data leadership, ensuring a sustainable and innovative future for your organisation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Data leadership and strategic utilisation of data |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the significance of data leadership in contemporary organisations \- Analyse the key principles of data management and governance for effective utilisation of data \- Develop a sound competitive positioning and a future-proof business strategy that aligns with your organisational vision and objectives  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 3:  |  Deep Dive into AI: From Fundamentals to Business Applications   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster your AI strategy building competency. Throughout the module, you will delve into the foundational principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). By examining a wide array of applications, including Machine Learning and Deep Learning, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of AI's relevance in diverse business contexts. The ultimate goal is to empower students to craft well-informed AI strategies that harness the power of machine learning and deep learning, to address specific business challenges effectively. By the end of this module, you will not only possess the analytical skills to evaluate AI's potential but will also be proficient in articulating the transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations, ensuring you can communicate their value effectively. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate the fundamental principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). \- Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. \- Formulate comprehensive AI strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. \- Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 3:  |  Deep Dive into AI: From Fundamentals to Business Applications   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster your AI strategy building competency. Throughout the module, you will delve into the foundational principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). By examining a wide array of applications, including Machine Learning and Deep Learning, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of AI's relevance in diverse business contexts. The ultimate goal is to empower students to craft well-informed AI strategies that harness the power of machine learning and deep learning, to address specific business challenges effectively. By the end of this module, you will not only possess the analytical skills to evaluate AI's potential but will also be proficient in articulating the transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations, ensuring you can communicate their value effectively. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate the fundamental principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). \- Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. \- Formulate comprehensive AI strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. \- Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 3:  |  Deep Dive into AI: From Fundamentals to Business Applications   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster your AI strategy building competency. Throughout the module, you will delve into the foundational principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). By examining a wide array of applications, including Machine Learning and Deep Learning, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of AI's relevance in diverse business contexts. The ultimate goal is to empower students to craft well-informed AI strategies that harness the power of machine learning and deep learning, to address specific business challenges effectively. By the end of this module, you will not only possess the analytical skills to evaluate AI's potential but will also be proficient in articulating the transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations, ensuring you can communicate their value effectively. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate the fundamental principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). \- Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. \- Formulate comprehensive AI strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. \- Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 3 Week 3 Content  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 3 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 3 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment  | Community Discussion:  The focus of this assignment is to analyze the diverse applications of AI, specifically Machine Learning, in various business contexts. By exploring real-world examples from the provided list of ML use cases, you will gain insight into how machine learning technologies are being employed to solve complex business problems.  Step 1: Selection of Machine Learning Use Case:  First, visit the provided website: ML Use Cases - Evidently AI (Hyperlink: https://www.evidentlyai.com/ml-system-design). Explore the list of machine learning use cases covering a wide array of industries and applications. Select one specific machine learning application that interests you the most or aligns closely with your career aspirations or industry focus.  Step 2: Analysis of Selected Use Case: \- Do some research on your selected machine learning use case. \- What is the business problem or challenge that the machine learning application aims to address. \- Describe the specific machine learning techniques or algorithms employed in the solution. \- What are the data sources utilized in the case?  \- What do you think are the performance criteria used to assess the effectiveness of the solution? \- Finally discuss the potential impact of the machine learning application on the business, including benefits, challenges, and limitations.  Read through other participants' responses as well, and respond to at least one person's analysis and ask a relevant question that can challenge their perspective. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Knowledge Check |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | isadora@elu.nl You can create the rubric using this LO: Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| week assignments build up to end-project |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 3:  |  Deep Dive into AI: From Fundamentals to Business Applications   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster your AI strategy building competency. Throughout the module, you will delve into the foundational principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). By examining a wide array of applications, including Machine Learning and Deep Learning, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of AI's relevance in diverse business contexts. The ultimate goal is to empower students to craft well-informed AI strategies that harness the power of machine learning and deep learning, to address specific business challenges effectively. By the end of this module, you will not only possess the analytical skills to evaluate AI's potential but will also be proficient in articulating the transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations, ensuring you can communicate their value effectively. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate the fundamental principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI). \- Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. \- Formulate comprehensive AI strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. \- Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
