| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 4:  | The Generative Journey: from "Attention is all you need" to Business Revolution |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Your journey in Module 4 commences with a transformative exploration of Generative AI, where you will acquire the indispensable skills and knowledge necessary for (Generative) AI strategy building. Throughout this module, you will grasp the foundational concepts of Generative AI, diving deep into its intricate principles and cutting-edge technologies. You will analyse real-world scenarios, gaining insights into how GenAI technologies are leveraged to conquer complex challenges. With this understanding, you will be prepared to confront specific business obstacles, crafting comprehensive plans that seamlessly integrate the power of Generative AI, paving the way for innovation and business revolution. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | (Generative) AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  |  Evaluate the fundamental principles of (Generative) Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). (Week 1) Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. (Week 2) Formulate AI business strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively. (Week 4)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 1 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment  | WEEK 1 Objective/focus: Build a 1-page pitch plan of a solution to incorporate Gen-AI in a travel vlogging platform Learning outcome: Understand, identify, and distinguish between business use cases and applications of Gen-AI that can lead to competitive advantage and digital transformation in organizations. Instructions:  Primeflix is a vlogging platform specialized in travel videos, where content creators can create their own channels and upload travel guides and tips in video format. - - - Content creators typically accompany their video uploads with text descriptions, reviews of places visited (e.g. hotels, restaurants, shops, museums), and supplementary visual material like pictures taken on their trips. \-        Meanwhile, end users or watchers can subscribe to creators’ channels, comment on videos, rate them, and also rate reviews and pictures uploaded together with videos. The objective is to propose a pitch plan for leveraging the use of Gen-AI solutions in benefit of one of the two types of users: content creators and watchers. \-        Choose one of the two user types you will analyze in this task. \-        Propose a business problem or need in this scenario, and a solution to address it through Gen-AI, such that the solution positively impacts your chosen user type. \-        You will briefly describe the problem scenario to target, the proposed solution, and the type(s) of Gen-AI tasks and architectures involved in the solution, as well as the business impact/benefits. You can optionally incorporate the combined use of Gen-AI with other conventional AI solutions. Guidelines: 1 Page document exported to PDF. Arial Format, size 11. Single line spacing. Resources: M4.1 Resources and workshop slides |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Knowledge Check | GEN-AI IN BUSINESS QUIZZES WEEK 1 Q1: Which of the following AI functions relates to Generative AI the most? \-        Optimizing delivery routes \-        Predicting sales \-        Creating social media content \-        Identifying customer segments Q2: Gen-AI models can generate new content that … \-        Mimics existing content and data \-        Looks original and creative \-        Looks completely real \-        Mimics natural language Q3: Most Gen-AI architectures are founded on … \-        Robotics \-        Classical machine learning models \-        Deep neural networks \-        Knowledge representation and reasoning Q4: Most common Gen-AI applications are associated with … \-        NLP and Robotics \-        Computer vision and NLP \-        Predictive machine learning \-        Sentiment analysis Q5: Which of the following deep learning architectures can be utilize to slightly change the eye color or size in a picture of yours? \-        Feed-forward neural network \-        Transformer \-        GAN \-        Variational autoencoder Q6: Transformers are the foundation architecture for … \-        Modern large-scale NLP applications \-        Stock market predictions \-        Generating fake images \-        Face recognition in videos Q7: Your company owns a small corpus of hundreds of insurance policy documents and data, but limited computing resources to build very large-scale AI solutions. They want to leverage an LLM to specialize in extracting answers to customer questions via a chatbot. Which approach should they follow? \-        LLM pre-training \-        LLM fine-tuning \-        Both of the above \-        None of the above Q8: Evaluating whether a detailed customer review of a restaurant is positive or negative involves a … task. \-        Summarization \-        Translation \-        Text generation \-        Sentiment analysis  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 4:  | The Generative Journey: from "Attention is all you need" to Business Revolution |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Your journey in Module 4 commences with a transformative exploration of Generative AI, where you will acquire the indispensable skills and knowledge necessary for (Generative) AI strategy building. Throughout this module, you will grasp the foundational concepts of Generative AI, diving deep into its intricate principles and cutting-edge technologies. You will analyse real-world scenarios, gaining insights into how GenAI technologies are leveraged to conquer complex challenges. With this understanding, you will be prepared to confront specific business obstacles, crafting comprehensive plans that seamlessly integrate the power of Generative AI, paving the way for innovation and business revolution. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | (Generative) AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  |  Evaluate the fundamental principles of (Generative) Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). (Week 1) Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. (Week 2) Formulate AI business strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively. (Week 4)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 2 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment  | Objective/focus: To apply prompt engineering principles and best practices to obtain an LLM outcome that approximates a desired result as much as possible. Learning outcome: To be able to apply effective prompt engineering principles in a conversational user-AI interaction process, so as to obtain an intended LLM outcome. Instructions:  Open ChatGPT 3.5 free version at: https://chat.openai.com/  Below are two examples of ChatGPT outputs with input prompt(s) being unknown. Your task this week consists in choosing one of the two examples in the screenshots, and writing a series of iterative prompts aimed at obtaining a final output that resembles the one in the chosen example as much as possible. During the process, be aware of the prompt engineering principles and tips learned in class and try your best to apply them. Example 1:   Example 2:    Guidelines: You can use an interaction sequence of 1-5 prompts to get as close as you can to either one of the two example outputs. Maximum limit is 5 prompts, and there should be a clear refinement process between consecutive prompts. If you manage to get a good and similar response with just 1 prompt, that’s also great\! What you need to submit:  •        The conversational flow with ChatGPTsequence, showing the 1-5 prompts supplied, along with the response to each one. •        An accompanying paragraph explaining your approach, highlighting the prompt engineering principles you applied based on what you learned in class. 1-2 Page document exported to PDF. Arial Format, size 11. Single line spacing. Assignment Resources: M4.2 Resources 1-4 and workshop slides  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Knowledge Check | WEEK 2 Q1: A prompt is a question or request formulated with the aim of … \-&#9;Getting a translated text \-&#9;Getting a product description \-&#9;Getting some information or insight \-&#9;Making a decision based on data Q2: Which of these four is not a key trait good prompts should have? \-&#9;Be specific \-&#9;Provide the context of the task \-&#9;Be concise \-&#9;Incorporate all the necessary information to get the response sought Q3: Complete this sentence: Models can receive \_\_\_ upon a response to a previous prompt in order to improve its next response. \-&#9;User likes/dislikes \-&#9;User feedback \-&#9;A dataset \-&#9;None of the above Q4: Select the prompt that most likely led to this answer: “The tallest tree species is the coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens), which is most common along the coast of northern California in the United States.” \-&#9;What is the tallest tree species in the world? \-&#9;In one sentence, what is the tallest tree species and where is it most common? \-&#9;Describe what is the tallest tree species and places where is it most common. \-&#9;Tell me about the tallest tree in the world. Q5: Which aspect best describes the benefits of incorporating prompt engineering practices in business? \-&#9;It leads to better and more informed decisions \-&#9;It can help promote fairness and bias removal in generated content \-&#9;It incentivizes personalization \-&#9;All are correct  Q6: Which one is not an example of multi-modal Gen-AI use case? \-&#9;Generate a fairy tale story upon an initial paragraph. \-&#9;Supply an image of a broken car glass along with a text request to process the car accident through an insurance company chatbot \-&#9;Provide a picture of yourself and a request to change your hairstyle \-&#9;Generate a synchronized musical video for a wedding, upon a set of images of the two event protagonists, and a song they both like. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 4:  | The Generative Journey: from "Attention is all you need" to Business Revolution |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Your journey in Module 4 commences with a transformative exploration of Generative AI, where you will acquire the indispensable skills and knowledge necessary for (Generative) AI strategy building. Throughout this module, you will grasp the foundational concepts of Generative AI, diving deep into its intricate principles and cutting-edge technologies. You will analyse real-world scenarios, gaining insights into how GenAI technologies are leveraged to conquer complex challenges. With this understanding, you will be prepared to confront specific business obstacles, crafting comprehensive plans that seamlessly integrate the power of Generative AI, paving the way for innovation and business revolution. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | (Generative) AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  |  Evaluate the fundamental principles of (Generative) Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). (Week 1) Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. (Week 2) Formulate AI business strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively. (Week 4)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 4:  | The Generative Journey: from "Attention is all you need" to Business Revolution |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Your journey in Module 4 commences with a transformative exploration of Generative AI, where you will acquire the indispensable skills and knowledge necessary for (Generative) AI strategy building. Throughout this module, you will grasp the foundational concepts of Generative AI, diving deep into its intricate principles and cutting-edge technologies. You will analyse real-world scenarios, gaining insights into how GenAI technologies are leveraged to conquer complex challenges. With this understanding, you will be prepared to confront specific business obstacles, crafting comprehensive plans that seamlessly integrate the power of Generative AI, paving the way for innovation and business revolution. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | (Generative) AI strategy building  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  |  Evaluate the fundamental principles of (Generative) Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). (Week 1) Analyse the diverse applications of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, in various business contexts. (Week 2) Formulate AI business strategies that leverage machine, deep learning, and generative AI capabilities to address specific business challenges. Communicate the value, potential, and transformative impact of AI strategies within organisations effectively. (Week 4)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 4 Knowledge Check | WEEK 4  Q1: Which of these refer to an established AI framework for instructional designers to experiment and integrate AI in their business? \-&#9;Taker, designer, shaper \-&#9;Getter, maker, shaper \-&#9;Taker, maker, shaper \-&#9;Thinker, maker, shaper Q2: Which of these elements is not indispensable in a robust Gen-AI leadership strategy? \-&#9;A solid understanding of the goals that drive the organization \-&#9;An identification of use cases to pursue the organization goals \-&#9;Identifying the right Gen-AI technologies to address the use cases \-&#9;Acquiring the services of a cloud provider for AI infrastructure Q3: One of these is not a subarea of Responsible AI. Can you find it? \-&#9;Explainable AI (XAI) \-&#9;AI Ethics and fairness \-&#9;Accountability and governance \-&#9;Prompt engineering Q4: An AI system for recommending hotels tends to list popular hotels from big brands at the top of search and recommendation lists for users, pushing smaller accommodations like guesthouses at the bottom. There is an issue with … \-&#9;Biased, unfair AI decisions \-&#9;Data protection breaches \-&#9;Lack of AI model interpretability \-&#9;High hotel occupancy and very expensive rates\! Q5: GDPR is … \-&#9;A regional regulation for safeguarding personal or sensitive data from inadequate use \-&#9;An AI regulatory Act proposed by the EU \-&#9;A modern data management system framework \-&#9;A set of government guidelines for promoting ethical development and use of data and AI systems Q6: A simple machine learning model like a decision tree for classification is an example of … \-&#9;Black-box model \-&#9;White-box model \-&#9;Grey-box model \-&#9;Accountable AI system Q7: The subarea responsible for defining mechanisms for mitigating and preventing the unauthorized or malicious use of AI systems is … \-&#9;AI accountability \-&#9;AI governance \-&#9;AI security \-&#9;AI ethics |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 5:  | Building Responsible & Ethical AI |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to develop the critical competency of ethical and responsible AI integration into business. Throughout this module, you will rigorously evaluate the ethical considerations entailed in AI implementation within business operations, with a focus on ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. You will delve into the analysis of potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies in a business context, promoting sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. Understanding AI governance and regulatory frameworks will be essential as you learn how to ensure that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards, minimising risks and fostering responsible AI use. Lastly, you will explore the concept of singularity and its potential impact on AI integration into business, preparing to address evolving ethical dilemmas and anticipate future challenges, thereby cultivating your expertise in responsible and ethical AI integration.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Ethical and responsible AI integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate ethical considerations associated with AI implementation in business operations, ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. \- Analyse the potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies within a business context, emphasising sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. \- Interpret AI governance and regulatory frameworks, ensuring that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards to minimise risks and promote responsible AI use.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1 Assignment  | \#\#\# Assignment Title: Ethical Principles and Bias in AI: A Hypothetical Case Study Approach  1\. \*\*Introduction:\*\* Acknowledge the dual-edged nature of AI — its potential to revolutionize industries and improve lives on one hand, and its ability to introduce biases and ethical concerns on the other. This assignment invites you to imagine a scenario where you'll deal directly with these ethical challenges. Your mission is to identify and address biases in an AI system you conceptualize, ensuring your approach is rooted in ethical principles like fairness, transparency, and accountability.  2\. \*\*Task:\*\*     - Choose an industry where AI is impactful and craft a fictional scenario that's ripe for ethical investigation, focusing on potential biases and ethical quandaries.    - Analyze this fictional AI system thoroughly to pinpoint potential biases and consider their effects on all parties involved.    - Utilize ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, and accountability to develop a set of strategies aimed at combating these biases. Your solutions should not only tackle the issues identified but also promote AI use that is in harmony with societal values and responsible innovation.  \*\*Guidelines:\*\*  This assignment challenges you to combine analytical depth with creative problem-solving. Successfully identifying biases and applying ethical principles in a fictional context is key. Your submission should clearly and comprehensively present your case study and solutions, showcasing your grasp of AI's ethical dimensions.  \*\*Submission Instructions:\*\* Submit your word (either a PDF or a Word document) in \~ 500-600 words. Approach this assignment with curiosity and a dedication to contributing thoughtfully to the discussion on ethical AI.  This narrative-style introduction is designed to prepare you for a reflective and critical examination of ethical issues in AI, encouraging deep engagement with the assignment’s goals. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Knowledge Check | 1\. What is a key challenge in ensuring fairness in AI systems?          • A) Increasing the speed of AI decision-making                  • B) Ensuring AI does not reinforce existing biases                  • C) Making AI systems more cost-effective                  • D) Enhancing the physical appearance of AI robots                  2. Why is transparency important in AI systems?                  • A) To make AI systems operate faster                  • B) To reduce the cost of AI development                  • C) To make the decision-making process understandable                  • D) To improve AI mobility and flexibility                  "3. In the case of Microsoft's ""Tay"" chatbot, which ethical consideration was breached?"                  • A) Cost-effectiveness                  • B) Accountability for offensive content                  • C) Speed of response                  • D) Physical durability                  4. How did the use of facial recognition technology by a popular social media platform raise privacy concerns?                  • A) By making the platform more difficult to navigate                  • B) By using facial recognition without adequate consent                  • C) By reducing the quality of social media content                  • D) By increasing the platform’s subscription fees                  5. What is a primary goal of Explainable AI (XAI)?                  • A) To make AI systems operate autonomously                  • B) To reduce the computational power needed for AI                  • C) To increase the transparency and understandability of AI decisions                  • D) To enhance the physical capabilities of robots                  6. Why are some AI systems referred to as ""black box"" algorithms?"                  • A) Because they are used in secure financial transactions                  • B) Because their decision-making processes are not easily understandable by humans                  • C) Because they are primarily used in confidential military operations                  • D) Because they operate mainly during nighttime          |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  |  \#\#\# Learning Outcome: Students will be able to evaluate ethical considerations associated with AI implementation in business operations, ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values.  \#\#\# Evaluation Criteria and Ratings:  \#\#\#\# Criterion 1: Understanding and Evaluation of Ethical Considerations \- \*\*5: Excellent\*\* - Demonstrates an exceptional understanding of ethical considerations in AI, with comprehensive analysis and insightful evaluation of biases and responsible practices. The analysis is deeply supported by nuanced examples and critical engagement with the subject matter. \- \*\*4: Between Very Good and Excellent\*\* \- \*\*3: Satisfactory\*\* - Displays a basic understanding of ethical considerations, with some analysis of biases and responsible practices. The evaluation is general and somewhat supported by examples, indicating a moderate level of engagement with the topic. \- \*\*2: Between Satisfactory and Poor\*\* \- \*\*1: Poor\*\* - Demonstrates a minimal understanding of ethical considerations, with scant analysis of biases and responsible practices. Insights are unsupported or irrelevant, indicating a lack of engagement with the assignment's objectives.  \#\#\#\# Criterion 2: Application of Ethical Principles to AI Case Study \- \*\*5: Excellent\*\* - Sophisticated application of ethical principles to the hypothetical AI case study, offering innovative and well-reasoned strategies to mitigate biases. Proposals demonstrate a deep understanding of ethical principles and their relevance to responsible AI practices. \- \*\*4: Between Very Good and Excellent\*\* \- \*\*3: Satisfactory\*\* - Basic application of ethical principles to the case study, with some strategies proposed to address biases. The application shows understanding but lacks depth and innovation in proposing solutions. \- \*\*2: Between Satisfactory and Poor\*\* \- \*\*1: Poor\*\* - Minimal or incorrect application of ethical principles to the case study, with few or no effective strategies proposed to mitigate biases. Demonstrates a lack of understanding of how ethical principles apply to AI challenges.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 5:  | Building Responsible & Ethical AI |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to develop the critical competency of ethical and responsible AI integration into business. Throughout this module, you will rigorously evaluate the ethical considerations entailed in AI implementation within business operations, with a focus on ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. You will delve into the analysis of potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies in a business context, promoting sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. Understanding AI governance and regulatory frameworks will be essential as you learn how to ensure that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards, minimising risks and fostering responsible AI use. Lastly, you will explore the concept of singularity and its potential impact on AI integration into business, preparing to address evolving ethical dilemmas and anticipate future challenges, thereby cultivating your expertise in responsible and ethical AI integration.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Ethical and responsible AI integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate ethical considerations associated with AI implementation in business operations, ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. \- Analyse the potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies within a business context, emphasising sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. \- Interpret AI governance and regulatory frameworks, ensuring that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards to minimise risks and promote responsible AI use.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 2 Assignment | \#\#\# Assignment Title: Navigating Environmental and Societal Impacts of AI: A Sustainable Development Challenge  1\. \*\*Introduction:\*\* Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds the power to transform our world, offering unprecedented opportunities for innovation across various sectors. However, this technological advancement comes with significant environmental and societal challenges, including resource depletion, energy consumption, and ethical dilemmas. In this assignment, you'll embark on a journey to explore these challenges. Your task is to envision a sustainable AI solution that addresses both environmental concerns and societal wellbeing, adhering to principles of sustainability, corporate responsibility, and ethical integrity.  2\. \*\*Task:\*\*     - \*\*Select Your Arena:\*\* Choose a domain (such as urban planning, agriculture, or healthcare) where AI can significantly impact environmental sustainability and societal health. Create a hypothetical scenario that highlights a problem in this domain where AI could be both part of the problem and the solution.    - \*\*Identify the Challenges:\*\* Analyze the environmental and societal implications of deploying AI in your chosen scenario. Identify specific challenges, such as energy consumption, carbon footprint, or societal disparities, that might arise from the implementation of AI technologies.    - \*\*Craft Your Solution:\*\* Drawing on ethical principles of sustainability, fairness, and transparency, propose an AI-based approach or solution that mitigates identified challenges. Your solution should aim to promote environmental conservation, enhance societal welfare, and ensure equitable benefits across communities.  \*\*Guidelines:\*\* This assignment encourages you to blend critical thinking with innovative problem-solving. It challenges you to scrutinize the dual impacts of AI — both as a potential contributor to environmental and societal issues and as a key player in solving these issues. Your response should be a detailed exposition of your case study, demonstrating a nuanced understanding of sustainable AI development and ethical considerations.  \*\*Submission Instructions:\*\* Please submit your response as a PDF or Word document, approximately 500-600 words in length. Approach this task with an investigative mindset, eager to explore the complexities of ethical AI implementation in the context of sustainability and societal well-being.  This assignment is structured to deepen your comprehension of the environmental and societal dimensions of AI, fostering a critical examination of how AI technologies can be developed and utilized responsibly for the greater good. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Knowledge Check |         1.        What is a significant environmental concern associated with the training of large AI models?         •        A) High energy consumption and CO2 emissions         •        B) Increased demand for skilled labor         •        C) Decreased internet speeds         •        D) Reduced global smartphone battery life         •        Correct Answer: A         2.        Which of the following is NOT a way AI can contribute to environmental sustainability?         •        A) Optimizing energy use in smart grids         •        B) Increasing the production of single-use plastics         •        C) Predicting climate change impacts         •        D) Enhancing recycling processes         •        Correct Answer: B         3.        What role does corporate responsibility play in the development and deployment of AI technologies?         •        A) Ensuring AI technologies are used primarily for entertainment         •        B) Focusing solely on maximizing short-term profits         •        C) Aligning AI implementation with ethical standards and societal values         •        D) Promoting AI technologies as the sole solution to social issues         •        Correct Answer: C         4.        Which technique is used to make AI models more energy-efficient?         •        A) Increasing the number of parameters         •        B) Decreasing algorithm accuracy         •        C) Expanding data center sizes         •        D) Model pruning         •        Correct Answer: D         5.        How can policy frameworks influence sustainable AI development?         •        A) Mandating the use of renewable energy in AI operations         •        B) By banning AI technologies         •        C) Encouraging the use of non-renewable energy sources         •        D) Discouraging research into energy efficiency         •        Correct Answer: A         6.        What is a challenge in achieving sustainable AI development?         •        A) Balancing model performance with computational efficiency         •        B) The reluctance to use AI in business operations         •        C) The abundance of renewable energy sources         •        D) The lack of interest in AI from the tech industry         •        Correct Answer: A         7.        Which of the following represents a public-private partnership’s role in sustainable AI?         •        A) Restricting data sharing between entities         •        B) Limiting AI research to private companies         •        C) Supporting the deployment of unsustainable AI technologies         •        D) Facilitating research and development of sustainable AI solutions         •        Correct Answer: D |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | \#\#\# Learning Outcome: Students will be able to develop and propose AI solutions that address environmental sustainability and societal wellbeing, grounded in ethical principles such as sustainability, fairness, and transparency.  \#\#\# Evaluation Criteria and Ratings:  \#\#\#\# Criterion 1: Analysis of Environmental and Societal Implications \- \*\*5: Excellent\*\* - Demonstrates an exceptional understanding of the environmental and societal implications of AI, with comprehensive analysis and insightful evaluation. The analysis is deeply supported by specific examples and demonstrates a critical engagement with the complexities of sustainable AI development. \- \*\*4: Between Very Good and Excellent\*\* \- \*\*3: Satisfactory\*\* - Shows a basic understanding of environmental and societal implications, with some analysis supported by examples. Indicates a moderate level of engagement with the topic and a general grasp of the challenges in sustainable AI development. \- \*\*2: Between Satisfactory and Poor\*\* \- \*\*1: Poor\*\* - Displays minimal understanding of the environmental and societal implications, with scant analysis or insight. Examples are unsupported or irrelevant, showing a lack of engagement with the assignment’s objectives.  \#\#\#\# Criterion 2: Development of Sustainable AI Solutions \- \*\*5: Excellent\*\* - Proposes innovative and well-reasoned AI solutions that effectively address identified environmental and societal challenges. Demonstrates a deep understanding of sustainability principles and their application in crafting responsible AI technologies. \- \*\*4: Between Very Good and Excellent\*\* \- \*\*3: Satisfactory\*\* - Offers basic AI solutions for the challenges identified, applying sustainability principles to a certain extent. Solutions show understanding but lack depth, creativity, or a comprehensive approach to sustainability. \- \*\*2: Between Satisfactory and Poor\*\* \- \*\*1: Poor\*\* - Provides minimal or superficial AI solutions with little to no effective application of sustainability principles. Demonstrates a lack of understanding in how to address environmental and societal challenges through AI.  \#\#\#\# Criterion 3: Integration of Ethical Principles in Solution Design \- \*\*5: Excellent\*\* - Excellently integrates ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, and accountability into the AI solution, demonstrating a nuanced approach to ethical AI design and deployment. \- \*\*4: Between Very Good and Excellent\*\* \- \*\*3: Satisfactory\*\* - Adequately integrates some ethical principles into the AI solution, though the application may lack depth or innovation. Shows a basic commitment to ethical considerations in AI design. \- \*\*2: Between Satisfactory and Poor\*\* \- \*\*1: Poor\*\* - Shows minimal or incorrect integration of ethical principles in the AI solution, indicating a misunderstanding of the importance of ethics in AI development and use.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 5:  | Building Responsible & Ethical AI |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to develop the critical competency of ethical and responsible AI integration into business. Throughout this module, you will rigorously evaluate the ethical considerations entailed in AI implementation within business operations, with a focus on ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. You will delve into the analysis of potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies in a business context, promoting sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. Understanding AI governance and regulatory frameworks will be essential as you learn how to ensure that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards, minimising risks and fostering responsible AI use. Lastly, you will explore the concept of singularity and its potential impact on AI integration into business, preparing to address evolving ethical dilemmas and anticipate future challenges, thereby cultivating your expertise in responsible and ethical AI integration.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Ethical and responsible AI integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate ethical considerations associated with AI implementation in business operations, ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. \- Analyse the potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies within a business context, emphasising sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. \- Interpret AI governance and regulatory frameworks, ensuring that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards to minimise risks and promote responsible AI use.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 3 Assignment  | Assignment Title: Designing Effective AI Governance Frameworks 1\. Introduction: Artificial Intelligence (AI) governance is essential for ensuring that AI technologies are developed and implemented in a manner that is safe, ethical, and beneficial to society. Effective AI governance addresses challenges related to transparency, accountability, ethical integrity, and regulatory compliance. In this assignment, you will develop a governance framework tailored to a specific industry and its unique challenges, focusing on maintaining innovation while safeguarding public interest and adhering to legal standards.  2\. Task:  Select Your Industry: Choose an industry (such as financial services, healthcare, automotive, or retail) where AI plays a transformative role. Describe a hypothetical scenario within this industry where AI governance is crucial. Identify Governance Challenges: Analyze the specific governance challenges in your chosen scenario. Consider issues like data privacy, bias and fairness, regulatory compliance, and the balance between innovation and ethical constraints. Develop Your Governance Framework: Propose a detailed AI governance framework for your scenario. Your framework should include guidelines on regulatory compliance, ethical AI usage, stakeholder engagement, and continuous monitoring and evaluation of AI systems. Consider the roles of various stakeholders, including AI developers, regulatory bodies, and end-users. Guidelines: This assignment requires you to integrate conceptual knowledge with practical application, encouraging a strategic approach to AI governance. It challenges you to design a framework that not only addresses current ethical and regulatory standards but also anticipates future developments and challenges in AI technology. Your response should detail how your governance framework will be implemented, monitored, and adapted over time.  Submission Instructions: Please submit your response as a PDF or Word document, approximately 500-600 words in length. Ensure your framework is clear, structured, and demonstrates a deep understanding of AI governance issues and solutions. Your analysis should reflect critical thinking and a grasp of the complexities involved in balancing technological advancement with ethical governance.  This assignment is designed to deepen your understanding of AI governance and its critical role in the ethical deployment of AI technologies across different sectors. It aims to foster a thoughtful examination of how AI can be guided to benefit society while addressing potential risks and ethical dilemmas. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Knowledge Check | 1\.        What is a primary goal of AI governance in healthcare? •        A) To maximize the speed of patient service •        B) To ensure ethical decision-making and protect patient data •        C) To automate all healthcare decisions •        D) To reduce healthcare costs as much as possible   2\.        What is a key focus of AI governance in autonomous vehicle technology? •        A) Enhancing entertainment systems in vehicles •        B) Ensuring safety and compliance with traffic laws •        C) Maximizing vehicle aesthetics •        D) Reducing production costs   3\.        How can fairness be ensured in AI-driven credit scoring systems? •        A) By exclusively using AI without human oversight •        B) By granting credit based on AI decisions alone •        C) By employing diverse datasets and regularly testing for biases •        D) By focusing on a single demographic   4\.     What is a significant challenge in AI-driven recruitment tools? •        A) Balancing the use of AI with privacy and bias concerns •        B) Eliminating human involvement in the hiring process •        C) Fully automating all recruitment activities •        D) Reducing the variety of job positions available   5\.        What type of regulatory compliance is crucial for AI systems handling consumer data? •        A) Data protection laws like GDPR and CCPA •        B) Environmental protection regulations •        C) Advertising standards •        D) Manufacturing regulations   6\.        What is a critical requirement of the EU AI Act for AI systems used in environmental conservation? •        A) Prioritizing short-term technological advancements •        B) Avoiding transparency with stakeholders •        C) Focusing on the profitability of AI technologies •        D) Ensuring AI systems do not harm the environment and comply with sustainability guidelines    7\.        How does the EU AI Act impact AI applications in healthcare? •        A) It mandates the complete replacement of human staff with AI •        B) It emphasizes on administrative tasks only •        C) It requires that AI systems improve patient safety and comply with strict ethical standards •        D) It focuses on reducing healthcare spending irrespective of outcomes   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Criterion 1: Analysis of Governance Challenges 5: Excellent - Provides a comprehensive and insightful analysis of AI governance challenges specific to the chosen industry, supported by detailed examples and demonstrating a deep understanding of the complexities involved in AI regulation and ethics. 4: Between Very Good and Excellent 3: Satisfactory - Presents a basic understanding of governance challenges with some analysis supported by relevant examples. Shows engagement with the topic and an understanding of common issues in AI governance. 2: Between Satisfactory and Poor 1: Poor - Offers minimal analysis of governance challenges, with little to no support from examples or relevant details. Shows a lack of engagement with the complexities of AI governance. Criterion 2: Development of AI Governance Framework 5: Excellent - Proposes a well-structured and innovative AI governance framework that effectively addresses the identified challenges. Demonstrates an advanced understanding of how to implement, monitor, and adapt governance mechanisms over time. 4: Between Very Good and Excellent 3: Satisfactory - Proposes a basic AI governance framework that addresses some challenges identified. The framework is adequately thought out but lacks depth or a detailed approach to implementation and adaptation. 2: Between Satisfactory and Poor 1: Poor - Provides a minimal or superficial governance framework with little to no effective strategy for addressing the governance challenges identified. Lacks understanding of how to develop a functional and adaptable governance framework. Criterion 3: Integration of Ethical Principles in Governance Design 5: Excellent - Excellently integrates ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, accountability, and stakeholder engagement into the governance framework, showing a nuanced and critical approach to ethical AI governance. 4: Between Very Good and Excellent 3: Satisfactory - Adequately integrates some ethical principles into the governance framework, but the application may lack depth, innovation, or a holistic approach. Shows a commitment to ethical considerations but may not fully capture all necessary aspects. 2: Between Satisfactory and Poor 1: Poor - Shows minimal or incorrect integration of ethical principles in the governance framework, indicating a lack of understanding of the critical role of ethics in AI governance. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 5:  | Building Responsible & Ethical AI |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to develop the critical competency of ethical and responsible AI integration into business. Throughout this module, you will rigorously evaluate the ethical considerations entailed in AI implementation within business operations, with a focus on ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. You will delve into the analysis of potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies in a business context, promoting sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. Understanding AI governance and regulatory frameworks will be essential as you learn how to ensure that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards, minimising risks and fostering responsible AI use. Lastly, you will explore the concept of singularity and its potential impact on AI integration into business, preparing to address evolving ethical dilemmas and anticipate future challenges, thereby cultivating your expertise in responsible and ethical AI integration.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Ethical and responsible AI integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Evaluate ethical considerations associated with AI implementation in business operations, ensuring alignment with responsible practices and societal values. \- Analyse the potential social and environmental consequences of AI technologies within a business context, emphasising sustainability, corporate responsibility, and positive societal contributions. \- Interpret AI governance and regulatory frameworks, ensuring that AI-driven business practices comply with legal and ethical standards to minimise risks and promote responsible AI use.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 4 Assignment  | Assignment Title: Ethical Governance and Strategic Preparation for AI Singularity Introduction: As artificial intelligence (AI) advances towards the singularity — the point at which AI surpasses human intelligence — it presents unique challenges and opportunities for businesses and society. This critical juncture could reshape industries, redefine human roles, and raise profound ethical questions. In this assignment, you will explore the concept of AI singularity, its potential impact on specific sectors, and the importance of preparing ethical governance frameworks to guide its development and integration. Task: \- Select Your Sector: Choose a specific industry (such as finance, healthcare, or public safety) where the impact of AI reaching singularity could be particularly transformative. Develop a hypothetical scenario that illustrates both the potential benefits and challenges of AI singularity in this sector. \- Identify the Challenges: Discuss the ethical, societal, and operational challenges that could emerge from AI achieving and operating at singularity within your chosen sector. Consider issues like decision-making autonomy, job displacement, and ethical dilemmas in AI-human interactions. \- Craft Your Solution: Propose a framework for ethical governance and strategic preparation that addresses these challenges. Your solution should include measures for ensuring transparency, accountability, and human-centered values in AI development. Suggest strategies for businesses and policymakers to proactively engage with these technologies, ensuring they contribute positively to society. \- Public Relations Strategy: Develop a public relations strategy that outlines how the company should communicate its AI initiatives to the public. This should include methods for building trust, explaining the benefits and risks of AI singularity, and engaging with stakeholders through transparent dialogue. Guidelines: This assignment challenges you to think critically about the future of AI and its intersection with human values and societal norms. It encourages a detailed analysis of how sectors can proactively prepare for significant technological shifts. Your response should be a comprehensive exploration of your scenario, underpinned by a robust ethical framework that highlights innovative and practical solutions, along with a strategic approach to public communication.  Submission Instructions: Please submit your response as a PDF or Word document, approximately 550-650 words in length. Aim to present a balanced view that considers both the potential of AI singularity to drive progress and the importance of safeguarding ethical and societal interests, while effectively managing public perceptions.  This assignment is designed to deepen your understanding of the complexities and responsibilities associated with guiding AI development as we approach the singularity, emphasizing the role of ethical foresight, strategic planning, and effective public relations in harnessing the benefits of AI while mitigating its risks. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Knowledge Check | Question 1: What is one major ethical concern with AI surpassing human intelligence? A) Increased energy consumption B) The ability to create artwork C) Decision-making autonomy D) Faster data processing  Question 2: Which economic model is proposed to support workers displaced by AI? A) Capital gains tax increase B) Higher property taxes C) Decreased corporate taxes D) Universal Basic Income  Question 3: What is a key risk of AI in legal systems? A) Inability to understand nuanced human contexts B) Faster court proceedings C) Reduced paperwork D) Increased transparency  Question 4: Asimov’s First Law of Robotics states: A) A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm. B) A robot must obey human orders unless they conflict with other laws. C) A robot must protect its own existence. D) A robot must improve its capabilities autonomously.  Question 5: Which strategy is used to mitigate existential risks posed by AI? A) Encouraging AI development B) Promoting AI in creative arts C) AI containment protocols D) Developing international regulations for safe AI development  Question 6: In healthcare, AI raises significant ethical dilemmas concerning: A) Privacy of genetic data B) Equitable access to advanced treatments C) All the options D) Improved diagnostic accuracy  Question 7: What global dynamics could the AI arms race affect? A) Decreased need for diplomacy B) International security C) Reduction in global travel D) Increased cultural exchanges  Question 8: What role could AI play in enhancing human capabilities? A) Reducing educational needs B) Simplifying languages C) Augmenting cognitive and physical abilities D) Decreasing physical activities  Question 9: What is essential to manage AI's impact on transportation? A) Reducing public transit options B) Increasing the cost of AI technology C) Ensuring safety protocols are fail-safe D) Limiting AI application to non-urban areas |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Criterion 1: Analysis of AI Singularity Impacts  5: Excellent - Provides a thorough and insightful analysis of the potential impacts of AI singularity in the chosen sector, supported by detailed examples and demonstrating a deep understanding of the complexities involved in AI advancements. 4: Between Very Good and Excellent 3: Satisfactory - Presents a basic understanding of the impacts with some analysis supported by relevant examples. Shows engagement with the topic. 2: Between Satisfactory and Poor 1: Poor - Provides minimal analysis of the impacts, with little to no support from examples or relevant details. Indicates a lack of engagement with the complexities of AI singularity. Criterion 2: Development of Practical Ethical Strategies  5: Excellent - Proposes a comprehensive and innovative strategy that effectively addresses the ethical, societal, and operational challenges identified in the scenario. Demonstrates a nuanced understanding of strategic planning and ethical considerations for AI at singularity levels. 4: Between Very Good and Excellent 3: Satisfactory - Proposes a clear strategy that addresses many of the challenges. The strategy is well thought out but may lack detail or innovative approaches to more complex issues. 2: Between Satisfactory and Poor 1: Poor - Offers a basic or underdeveloped strategy that fails to effectively address the identified challenges. Shows limited understanding of the complexities of ethical and strategic planning in AI applications. Criterion 3: Public Relations Strategy Development  5: Excellent - Develops a robust public relations strategy that effectively communicates AI initiatives, builds public trust, and engages stakeholders through transparent dialogue. Demonstrates deep insight into managing public perceptions and expectations. 4: Between Very Good and Excellent 3: Satisfactory - Creates an adequate public relations strategy that somewhat addresses the need for transparency and public engagement but lacks innovation or comprehensive stakeholder management. 2: Between Satisfactory and Poor 1: Poor - Provides a minimal or superficial public relations strategy, inadequately addressing the need to manage public perceptions or engage with stakeholders effectively. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 6:  | ELECTIVE (Self-Paced)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 6 of the Tech MBA programme offers you the opportunity to tailor your learning experience by selecting an elective technology track from RPA, VR/AR, Blockchain, or IoT, all aligned with the overarching target competency of technology integration into business. This self-paced module empowers you to assess the strategic value of your chosen technology within the context of a business, encouraging critical analysis of the potential impact on organisational processes and outcomes. Furthermore, you will develop strategies for the effective and sustainable integration of your chosen technology across diverse business domains. A key outcome of this module is your ability to proficiently present the rationale and potential outcomes of technology integration initiatives, with a specific focus on your selected technology.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Technology integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the strategic value of the selected technology within a business context. \- Analyse the potential impact of technology integration on organisational processes and outcomes. \- Formulate strategies for the effective and sustainable integration of the chosen technology into diverse business domains.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
