| week assignments build up to end-project |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 6:  | ELECTIVE (Self-Paced)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 6 of the Tech MBA programme offers you the opportunity to tailor your learning experience by selecting an elective technology track from RPA, VR/AR, Blockchain, or IoT, all aligned with the overarching target competency of technology integration into business. This self-paced module empowers you to assess the strategic value of your chosen technology within the context of a business, encouraging critical analysis of the potential impact on organisational processes and outcomes. Furthermore, you will develop strategies for the effective and sustainable integration of your chosen technology across diverse business domains. A key outcome of this module is your ability to proficiently present the rationale and potential outcomes of technology integration initiatives, with a specific focus on your selected technology.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Technology integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the strategic value of the selected technology within a business context. \- Analyse the potential impact of technology integration on organisational processes and outcomes. \- Formulate strategies for the effective and sustainable integration of the chosen technology into diverse business domains.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| week assignments build up to end-project |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MODULE 6:  | ELECTIVE (Self-Paced)  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 6 of the Tech MBA programme offers you the opportunity to tailor your learning experience by selecting an elective technology track from RPA, VR/AR, Blockchain, or IoT, all aligned with the overarching target competency of technology integration into business. This self-paced module empowers you to assess the strategic value of your chosen technology within the context of a business, encouraging critical analysis of the potential impact on organisational processes and outcomes. Furthermore, you will develop strategies for the effective and sustainable integration of your chosen technology across diverse business domains. A key outcome of this module is your ability to proficiently present the rationale and potential outcomes of technology integration initiatives, with a specific focus on your selected technology.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Technology integration into business  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Assess the strategic value of the selected technology within a business context. \- Analyse the potential impact of technology integration on organisational processes and outcomes. \- Formulate strategies for the effective and sustainable integration of the chosen technology into diverse business domains.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 7 - Week1:  | Understanding and Dealing with Change / wk1: Understand the Concept of Change Management |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In Module 7 you will be equipped with the essential competency of change management. You will learn about the principles, strategies, and tools of change management, helping you proficiently analyse the impact of change and discuss  comprehensive change management plans. You will gain understanding in identifying and addressing sources of resistance to change within organisations, necessary for facilitating smooth transitions. You will also learn to evaluate and select the most appropriate change management frameworks to guide organisational change efforts. Moreover, you will develop strategies to support organisational resilience in dynamic environments, ensuring that businesses can adapt and thrive in the face of change.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 7 Learning Outcomes | Wk1 - Demonstrate understanding of change management principles, strategies, and tools to analyse the impact of change and develop comprehensive change management plans.  Wk2 - Evaluate and select appropriate change management frameworks and apply them to guide organisational change efforts.  Wk3 - Identify and address sources of resistance to change within organisations, leveraging effective strategies and communication. Wk4 - Develop strategies to enhance organisational resilience in dynamic environments. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Change management   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Workshop Outline | 1-) Introduction to Change Management: •       Definition and importance of change management •       Key concepts and theories in change management •       The role of change management in organizations 2-) Change Management Principles and Strategies: •       Principles of effective change management •       Strategies for successful change implementation •       Analyzing the impact of change on organizations 3-) Tools and Techniques for Change Management: •       Overview of change management tools (e.g., SWOT analysis, stakeholder analysis) •       Techniques for planning and executing change •       Case studies on successful change management initiatives |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 1 Assignment: Change Management Case Analysis: XYZ Corporation's Transformation Journey | Instructions:  Read the provided case study of XYZ Corporation's transformation journey provided below.  Apply the concepts learned in the first week of the "Change Management" module to analyze the case and provide recommendations. Write a comprehensive report addressing the following points: \- Define what change management is and explain the importance of change management in an organizational context, using XYZ Corp as an example. \- Identify and analyze the internal change drivers (eg siloed organizational structures, bureaucratic decision-making) and external change drivers (eg shifting consumer trends, intensifying competition) that necessitated the transformation at XYZ Corporation. \- Compare and contrast Lewin's Change Management Model, Kotter's 8-Step Process, and the ADKAR Model. Evaluate the suitability of each model for guiding XYZ Corporation's change journey. \- Based on your analysis, recommend the most appropriate change management model(s) for XYZ Corporation and justify your choice with specific reasons and evidence from the case study.. \- Provide specific recommendations for XYZ Corporation to effectively manage its transformation journey, consider the identified change drivers and selected change management model(s) in your recommendations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 1 Assignment: Change Management Case Analysis: XYZ Corporation's Transformation Journey | XYZ Corporation, a leading player in the automotive industry, embarked on a transformation journey to remain competitive in the rapidly evolving market landscape. The company faced various internal and external challenges, including outdated technology infrastructure, changing consumer preferences, and intensifying competition from emerging market players.  Internally, XYZ Corporation struggled with siloed organizational structures and bureaucratic decision-making processes, hindering agility and innovation. Externally, shifting consumer trends towards electric vehicles and sustainable mobility solutions posed significant challenges for the traditional automotive manufacturer.  In response to these challenges, XYZ Corporation initiated a comprehensive transformation program aimed at modernizing its operations, diversifying its product portfolio, and enhancing customer experience. The transformation program encompassed various initiatives, including digitalization of manufacturing processes, development of electric vehicle prototypes, and implementation of customer-centric service models.  Throughout the transformation journey, XYZ Corporation leveraged change management principles and methodologies to navigate complexities and ensure successful implementation of initiatives. The company adopted a phased approach, engaging employees at all levels, fostering a culture of collaboration and innovation, and aligning strategic objectives with organizational values.  Despite initial resistance and challenges, XYZ Corporation achieved significant milestones in its transformation journey, including the launch of innovative products, expansion into new markets, and improved customer satisfaction ratings. The company's commitment to change management principles played a pivotal role in driving sustainable growth and maintaining competitive advantage in the dynamic automotive industry. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week 1 Assignment: Change Management Case Analysis: XYZ Corporation's Transformation Journey | Submission Guidelines: Your report should be typed and formatted according to academic writing standards. Provide clear explanations and rationale for your recommendations, supported by evidence from the case study and relevant literature. The report should be approximately 500-700 words in length, excluding references and appendices. Use APA style for citing sources and references. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Criteria 1: Understanding of Change Management  (20 points):  •        Excellent: Demonstrates a clear understanding of change management principles and their importance in an organizational context. •        Proficient: Shows a solid understanding of change management concepts with some minor gaps or inaccuracies. •        Adequate: Demonstrates a basic understanding of change management concepts but lacks depth or clarity. •        Needs Improvement: Shows limited understanding of change management concepts, with significant gaps in knowledge or understanding. •        Unsatisfactory : Fails to demonstrate understanding of change management concepts.  Criteria 2: Analysis of Change Drivers (20 Points) •        Excellent: Effectively identifies and analyzes internal and external change drivers based on the case study. •        Proficient: Offers a solid analysis of change drivers, identifying key factors and discussing their relevance to the transformation journey. •        Adequate : Provides a basic analysis of change drivers, identifying some relevant factors but lacking depth or insight. •        Needs Improvement : Shows limited analysis of change drivers, with minimal identification of relevant factors and little insight into their impact. •        Unsatisfactory: Fails to analyze change drivers or identify relevant factors.  Criteria 3: Comparison of Change Management Models (20 points) •        Excellent: Provides a thorough comparison and contrast of Lewin's, Kotter's, and ADKAR models. and Evaluates the suitability of each model for XYZ Corporation. •        Proficient: Provides a solid evaluation of change models, discussing their strengths and weaknesses and assessing their relevance to the case study. •        Adequate: Offers a basic evaluation of change models, identifying key features and discussing their potential applicability to the transformation journey. •        Needs Improvement: Shows limited evaluation of change models, with minimal discussion of their strengths, weaknesses, or applicability. •        Unsatisfactory: Fails to evaluate change models or discuss their relevance to the case study.  Criteria 4: Recommendation and Justification (20 points) •        Excellent: Recommends the most appropriate change management model(s) for XYZ Corporation. and Provides a well-reasoned justification supported by evidence from the case study. •        Proficient: Offers solid recommendations for change management strategies, supported by analysis but may lack depth or originality. •        Adequate: Provides basic recommendations for change management strategies, but they may lack specificity or may not be fully supported by analysis. •        Needs Improvement: Shows limited recommendations for change management strategies, with little connection to analysis or evaluation. •        Unsatisfactory: Fails to provide recommendations for change management strategies.  Criteria 5: Specific Recommendations for Managing Transformation (20 points) •        Excellent: Offers specific and actionable recommendations for managing XYZ Corporation’s transformation journey. and Considers identified change drivers and selected change management model(s). •        Proficient: Meets most academic writing standards with some minor errors or inconsistencies in formatting or referencing. •        Adequate: Demonstrates basic academic writing skills but lacks consistency or clarity in presentation. •        Needs Improvement: Shows significant deficiencies in academic writing skills, with frequent errors in formatting, referencing, or organization. •        Unsatisfactory: Fails to meet academic writing standards.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Wk1 Knowledge Check | Introduction to Change Management: What is the primary goal of change management in an organizational context? A) To reduce the number of employees B) To ensure that changes are implemented smoothly and successfully C) To increase the production rate D) To eliminate competition  Which of the following best describes the importance of change management? A) It helps in maintaining the status quo B) It reduces the need for training employees C) It ensures that changes align with organizational goals and minimize resistance D) It eliminates the need for leadership in organizations  Change management is primarily concerned with managing which aspect of an organization? A) Financial resources B) Technological advancements C) Human aspects and organizational processes D) Physical infrastructure  Change Drivers: Which of the following is an example of an internal change driver? A) New government regulations B) Emerging market trends C) Changes in consumer preferences D) Organizational restructuring  Which external factor can necessitate organizational change? A) Employee skill gaps B) Internal communication breakdowns C) Technological advancements D) Corporate culture  Why is it important to identify change drivers in change management? A) To maintain existing organizational structures B) To eliminate the need for employee training C) To understand the reasons for change and effectively plan the change process D) To avoid the change process altogether  Change Models: \*\*What are the three stages of Lewin's Change Management Model What are the three stages of Lewin's Change Management Model? A) Preparation, Implementation, and Review B) Unfreeze, Change, and Refreeze C) Planning, Execution, and Monitoring D) Initiation, Development, and Completion  Which step in Kotter's 8-Step Process involves creating a sense of urgency? A) Communicating the Vision B) Creating a Vision for Change C) Building a Guiding Coalition D) Establishing a Sense of Urgency  In the ADKAR model, what does the "R" stand for? A) Reinforcement B) Readiness C) Reorganization D) Realignment  Which change management model emphasizes the importance of engaging and empowering employees at all levels? A) Lewin's Change Management Model B) Kotter's 8-Step Process C) ADKAR Model D) McKinsey 7-S Model |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Present your strategy in the form of a written report, including a detailed implementation plan, and provide a justification for your strategic choices. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Assignment: Emerging Technologies Evaluation (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Explore the Gartner Hype Cycle and select three emerging technologies that are in different phases of the cycle (e.g., innovation trigger, peak of inflated expectations, plateau of productivity). |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and evaluate the potential applications, benefits, and challenges associated with each of the chosen technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create an infographic or visual presentation summarizing your findings and present it to the class, highlighting the technology's current stage and its implications for businesses. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 7 - Week2:  | Understanding and Dealing with Change / Wk2: Understand Change Planning Process |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In Module 7 you will be equipped with the essential competency of change management. You will learn about the principles, strategies, and tools of change management, helping you proficiently analyse the impact of change and discuss  comprehensive change management plans. You will gain understanding in identifying and addressing sources of resistance to change within organisations, necessary for facilitating smooth transitions. You will also learn to evaluate and select the most appropriate change management frameworks to guide organisational change efforts. Moreover, you will develop strategies to support organisational resilience in dynamic environments, ensuring that businesses can adapt and thrive in the face of change.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 7 Learning Outcomes | Wk1- Demonstrate understanding of change management principles, strategies, and tools to analyse the impact of change and develop comprehensive change management plans.  Wk2 - Evaluate and select appropriate change management frameworks and apply them to guide organisational change efforts.  Wk3 - Identify and address sources of resistance to change within organisations, leveraging effective strategies and communication. Wk4 - Develop strategies to enhance organisational resilience in dynamic environments.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Change management   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Workshop Outline | 1-) Essential Steps for an Effective Change Management: \- Assess Need – Create Sense of Urgency \- Build a guiding coalition \- Define Change Objective & Strategy \- Stakeholder Analysis & Engagement \- Developing Change Plan \- Implementation \- Monitoring & Adjusting \- Sustaining Change with Learnings 2-) Role & Responsibilities of Change Manager |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 7 Week 2 Content  |  https://hbr.org/2004/12/leading-change-when-business-is-good  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FlP1-5WMyo   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment Learning outcome | Evaluate and select appropriate change management frameworks and apply them to guide organisational change efforts.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assignment | Case Study: Blockbuster and the Rise of Streaming Services Company: Blockbuster LLC (Blockbuster)  Industry: Video Rental  Situation: Blockbuster, once a dominant force in the video rental industry, faced a significant threat in the late 1990s with the rise of streaming services like Netflix.  This new technology offered customers a more convenient and cost-effective way to access movies and TV shows, directly challenging Blockbuster's traditional brick-and-mortar model.  Problem: Blockbuster's business model relied on late fees, in-store rentals, and a limited selection of titles.  The company initially underestimated the disruptive potential of streaming services and was slow to adapt.  Learning Objectives:  Analyze the challenges faced by Blockbuster due to technological disruption. Create a sense of urgency Apply Kotter's 8-Step Change Management Model to develop a plan for Blockbuster to adapt to the streaming revolution. Discuss the potential benefits and risks associated with the proposed change plan. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Criteria 1: Understanding of Change Planning (25 points): •        Discusses the steps involved in planning change initiatives, including goal setting, stakeholder analysis, and risk assessment. •        Explains the relevance of these steps in the context of GreenTech Inc.'s sustainability initiative.  Criteria 2:Evaluation of Communication Strategies (25 points): •        Evaluates the effectiveness of change communication strategies employed by GreenTech Inc. •        Provides evidence-based analysis of how these strategies engaged stakeholders and fostered support.  Criteria 3: Analysis of Leadership Role (25 points): •        Analyzes the role of leadership in driving and supporting the sustainability initiative. •        Identifies key leadership behaviors and practices that contributed to the initiative's success.  Criteria 4: Recommendations (25 points): •        Provides specific and actionable recommendations for enhancing GreenTech Inc.'s change planning, communication, and leadership strategies. •        Justifies recommendations with evidence from the case study and relevant literature.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Wk2 Knowledge Check | Change Planning Process:s:  What is the primary objective of the change planning process? A) To minimize costs B) To outline the steps and strategies necessary for implementing change C) To recruit new employees D) To increase product sales  Which of the following is NOT a typical step in the change planning process? A) Defining the vision and goals B) Analyzing stakeholders C) Implementing change without feedback D) Creating a detailed action plan  Importance of Effective Change Communication: Why is effective change communication important in change management? A) It ensures that only managers are aware of the changes B) It reduces uncertainty and resistance among employees C) It delays the implementation of changes D) It eliminates the need for training  Which of the following is a key element of effective change communication? A) Using technical jargon B) Providing clear, consistent, and transparent information C) Restricting information to top management D) Avoiding discussions about the change  Communication Strategies for Change Management  What is a crucial aspect of developing communication strategies for change management? A) Excluding feedback mechanisms B) Considering the needs and concerns of all stakeholders C) Limiting communication to written memos D) Avoiding technology in communication  Which communication channel is often most effective for change management? A) Email only B) Face-to-face meetings, supplemented by digital communication C) Public announcements D) Written reports  Role of Change Leadership:  What is a primary role of change leadership in managing change? A) Ignoring employee concerns B) Providing vision, guidance, and support throughout the change process C) Focusing solely on operational tasks D) Delegating all responsibilities to middle management  Why is leadership important in change initiatives? A) Leaders can force change without resistance B) Leaders inspire and motivate employees to embrace change C) Leaders avoid direct communication with employees D) Leaders prioritize their personal goals over organizational goals  Collaboration and Teamwork:  How can enhancing collaboration and teamwork benefit change initiatives? A) By increasing individual workloads B) By fostering a sense of ownership and shared responsibility among employees C) By creating more hierarchical structures D) By isolating departments from one another  Which of the following is a strategy to enhance collaboration during change? A) Limiting team interactions B) Encouraging open communication and teamwork C) Assigning all tasks to a single individual D) Avoiding team-building activities |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 7:  Week 3 | Understanding and Dealing with Change / Wk3: Common Challenges of Change Management |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In Module 7 you will be equipped with the essential competency of change management. You will learn about the principles, strategies, and tools of change management, helping you proficiently analyse the impact of change and discuss  comprehensive change management plans. You will gain understanding in identifying and addressing sources of resistance to change within organisations, necessary for facilitating smooth transitions. You will also learn to evaluate and select the most appropriate change management frameworks to guide organisational change efforts. Moreover, you will develop strategies to support organisational resilience in dynamic environments, ensuring that businesses can adapt and thrive in the face of change.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 7 Learning Outcomes | Wk1- Demonstrate understanding of change management principles, strategies, and tools to analyse the impact of change and develop comprehensive change management plans.  Wk2 - Evaluate and select appropriate change management frameworks and apply them to guide organisational change efforts.  Wk3 - Identify and address sources of resistance to change within organisations, leveraging effective strategies and communication. Wk4 - Develop strategies to enhance organisational resilience in dynamic environments. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Change management   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Workshop Outline | 1-) Leadership vs. Management in Change Initiatives: •       Importance of leadership in driving change •       Common pitfalls in change management •       Balancing leadership and management roles 2-) Identifying Sources of Resistance: •       Internal sources (organizational culture, employee resistance) •       External sources (market conditions, regulatory changes) •       Methods for analyzing resistance to change 3-) Strategies to Overcome Resistance: •       Communication and engagement strategies •       Training and support mechanisms •       Leadership and influence techniques •       Continuous feedback and adaptation strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 7 Week 3 Content  | •        https://www.forbes.com/sites/billfischer/2016/03/26/the-leadership-advantage-of-bezos-musk-ma-and-zhang-an-explorers-mindset/?sh=519296b87046  •        https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=40meQNZl3KU   •        https://hbr.org/1995/05/leading-change-why-transformation-efforts-fail-2?utm\_medium=paidsearch\&utm\_source=google\&utm\_campaign=intlcontent\_leadership\&utm\_term=Non-Brand\&tpcc=intlcontent\_leadership\&gad\_source=1\&gclid=Cj0KCQjw\_-GxBhC1ARIsADGgDjshDIR1ZvypDwUP6pOTm52B7UiPlGMDu963PJko7UET63fXTq\_jPVAaAnm5EALw\_wcB  •        https://hbr.org/2005/10/the-hard-side-of-change-management  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment  Learning Outcome | \- Identify and address sources of resistance to change within organisations, leveraging effective strategies and communication. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | Read the provided case study on the Daffodil Inn. Review the concepts covered in the third week of the Change Management module, focusing on managing resistance to change. Write a comprehensive report addressing the following points: 1-) Identify Sources of Resistance: Discuss the sources of resistance to change at Daffodil Inn, both from employees and management and Use specific examples from the case study to illustrate these sources of resistance.  2-) Effective Strategies to Manage Resistance: Identify and discuss effective strategies to manage resistance to change that could be employed at Daffodil Inn. and Explain how these strategies can help address the identified sources of resistance.   3-) Lessons Learned: Reflect on the lessons that can be learned from the case study about managing resistance to change and Discuss how these lessons can be applied to more complex and challenging environments.    4-) Application of Mapping Tools: Apply the following mapping tools to the Daffodil Inn case, Gap Analysis to Outline the ‘As Is’ and ‘To Be’ conditions for the change at Daffodil Inn in a two-column Gap Analysis and Create an Iceberg image of the ‘As Is’ and ‘To Be’ factors, including above and below the waterline elements.  Use Force Field Analysis to Create a two-column Force Field Analysis diagram listing the forces for and against the change at Daffodil Inn, rating each force from 1-5 and Divide the forces into those above and below the waterline using the Iceberg diagram.  Use Route Analysis to Determine if Daffodil Inn is towards the start or at the end of the initial preparatory stage of change (unfreezing stage). and to Identify the key elements of preparing for change (unfreezing) that Deborah has managed to achieve so far. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | The case describes a change situation confronting the 4-star Daffodil hotel facing challenges such as increasing vacancy rates and employee turnover. The hotel prides itself on being a warm and friendly environment but is experiencing resistance to necessary changes. Issues include Resistance to Change: Concerns about outdated facilities, rising employee turnover, and lack of incentives have led to resistance from both employees and management.  Communication Challenges: Discussions between managers highlight differing opinions on the urgency and necessity of changes.  Leadership and Employee Engagement: The leadership style and employee engagement practices at Daffodil Inn are contributing to the resistance. In this study exercise, we move away from larger scale more celebrated cases. This is deliberate. We take a look at the day-to-day actions of Deborah, Jim and Jade, three managers in the Daffodil Inn hotel. It allows you to test your understanding of how to apply the mapping tools in an accessible smaller-scale situation. Once you have read through and applied the tools to this case, the Week 3 graded quiz will allow you to test your understanding. This will prepare you for applying the tools later on in more complex and challenging environments. Good luck\!   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | Daffodil Inn is a medium-sized, four-star hotel with 74 air-conditioned rooms, all with free wifi and free parking on site. All rooms have a small desk, a refrigerator and a tea and coffee maker, as well as a bathroom with a hairdryer and free toiletries. Its restaurant offers woodfired pizzas and a barbecue area with outdoor seating. It sells a wide range of beers, wines and cocktails. Daffodil Inn also has an indoor swimming pool and a fitness centre with plenty of facilities, including workout sessions at weekends. Jade Green is the hotel’s general manager, and she has two departmental managers reporting to her, as well as 23 other employees. Jade and the other senior managers have all worked at Daffodil in those roles for the past five years. The hotel prides itself on being a warm and friendly environment for customers and employees alike. Employees’ performances are not overly monitored, with the expectation that all employees will do the right thing, which is mostly the case. To maintain the highest levels of quality, a deep room cleaning and facilities maintenance programme is carried out every fortnight. This programme is managed and supervised by two experienced and highly dedicated housekeepers. A traditional reward system provides no monetary incentive beyond tipping, which is virtually nonexistent.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | A conversation with Jade Deborah’s concern was chiefly the vacancy rate. The number of empty hotel rooms had been growing for some time. Figures from the previous quarter showed that 32% of the rooms had been vacant. Occupancy rates were down 4% on the same time last year. What was worse was that other four-star hotels in the area didn’t seem to have the same trouble. The level of employee turnover had also started to rise. In a business that prided itself on unusually low turnover, this was ringing alarm bells for Deborah. She looked at her watch, and decided that she just had time to see Jade before she left for the day. ‘Hi, Jade,’ she said, with a smile. ‘I hope you don’t mind me coming down, but I’m really getting quite worried. I think we need an upgrade on some of our facilities. I’ve been looking at our vacancy rates, and I’m worried that if we don’t, the hotel will come under even more pressure. We really need a refurb to keep us competitive in the market. Jade frowned. ‘I understand where you’re coming from, but we really don’t have any spare capital right now. I can’t help thinking that this isn’t very urgent right now.’ ‘But that’s just it,’ Deborah replied. ‘The staff are getting worried about this, and they’re starting to leave. Not enough is done about upgrading facilities, or even keeping them up to date. Even the TVs are all out of date. Service and facilities is what brings customers back.’ Jade said, abruptly and rather sharply, ‘Staff turnover is a completely separate issue and I don’t see that it has anything to do with capital investment. What’s more,’ she added, ‘our hotel still performs better than plenty of others.’ ‘But we need to continue building for the future and we’ve always prided ourselves on unusually low turnover and new facilities,’ Deborah pointed out. ‘We can’t do that just now.’ Jade’s mobile started to ring. She reached for it, and Deborah turned away to see a customer entering the otherwise empty reception area. She moved to greet him. The conversation was over.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | A conversation with Jim A few days later, Deborah was having coffee with Jim, the HR manager. She remarked to him that there were rumours that several employees planned to leave and go to other hotels in the area. Jim had only been in the job a few months, but already he had been involved in sorting out several disputes, between individuals and departments. He was also finding that he was being used as a sounding board in hotel as well as personal problems. ‘Mmm,’ he responded thoughtfully to Deborah. ‘I’ve heard those rumours too. It’s certainly true that turnover is increasing. That’s usually a sign of organizational problems, but I don’t know if that’s the case here.’ Jim had always thought that high employee retention rates were important in any customer service business. The familiarity that develops between staff and customers cannot be bought or learned. He knew that losing that would have a direct and negative impact on almost everyone in the hotel. Given Deborah’s concern, he decided that it was definitely part of his job to take a quiet look at some turnover figures and see what he could discover.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | Some surprising news Jim found himself shocked by the figures. The hotel had a staff turnover rate of almost 40% over the past 18 months. Jim had little doubt that this was impairing customer relationships. He, too, decided that he would have to talk to Jade. However, Jim was a little surprised at Jade’s reaction to his figures. ‘Don’t worry,’ she said. ‘I’m sure it’s not a big issue. This will go away; you need to know that the hotel industry has always suffered from people moving from one place to another.' ‘Oh,’ said Jim, slightly nonplussed. ‘Everyone is tired,’ Jade went on. ‘This always happens at this time of year. By the time Christmas comes around and we have a couple of quiet weeks, everyone will settle down.’ Jim was a little taken aback by these comments, but didn’t want to disagree with his general manager, so he simply replied ‘Okay, you’re the boss.’ But he wasn’t sure he really wanted to leave it there. Perhaps he could talk to Deborah? Later that day, Jim remarked to Deborah that he was genuinely concerned about employee welfare. Many of the employees had mentioned to him that they found their jobs were becoming repetitive and sometimes dreary. This was particularly concerning in customer-facing jobs. Deborah replied, ‘I think that the structure might be a bit top-down. It’s making some of the employees feel that they don’t have any power or chance to take any initiative. Housekeeping is organized so that each housekeeper is supposed to be responsible for a particular 12–16 rooms, and they’re not supposed to swap them around. But they all know it takes longer to clean a room when the guest has checked out than a stayover, so some of them end up with too much work, and some with not enough. That just makes them frustrated, and it’s even worse if they have hotel management qualifications, because they’d really like more of a challenge.’ ‘Two of the staff came to see me to ask for a reference,’ Jim replied. ‘When I asked them why, Kylie said “I really like working here but beyond a pat on the back there is no incentive to do better, I just do what I am told.” She’s good. And I’ve seen John going out of his way to check wi-fi connections for a last-minute conference. It will be a real shame if we lose either of them. When John came to see me the other day, I asked him about his job, and he said, “I really like it here and the fact that it is so relaxed, but I don’t have any control over my day-to-day job, I just don’t feel invested in the hotel and it is affecting my motivation, which is not how I like to be.” And you know, I understand that.’ ‘Me too,’ Deborah agreed with a smile. ‘Here’s one closer to home for you,’ Jim went on. ‘I had someone come to me the other day. She wanted to talk about how to deal with the way her housekeeping supervisors go around checking on her work all the time. She didn’t want to say anything to them, in case it upset them, but it was bothering her enough that she was thinking about leaving. I’m not sure our “no conflict” norm is helping. If anything, it seems to have resulted in concerns not being flagged up and motivations being ignored. She said she thought that housekeepers should trust the work done by junior staff. I’m wondering if we should be thinking about how to help our senior housekeepers assume more of a coaching role, and move away from this topdown thinking.’ Deborah agreed that this might work. She remarked that she had noticed that her experienced housekeepers were becoming less flexible with roster requests, and were particularly cross at being asked to work at short notice. There were also fewer more junior staff who were showing signs of being keen to help one another out and work as a team.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| \[merged\] Week3 Assignment | Finding a way forward ‘I wonder if the issue is that staff and supervisors aren’t really paying attention to each other,’ Jim mused. ‘It seems to me that senior and junior staff are both upset. I hope they’re not taking this out on the customers, though I bet some of them are at least.’ ‘And I bet the staff could tell us what is wrong,’ Deborah said. ‘I think perhaps we should start to do a bit more listening, or maybe set them up to listen a bit more.’ ‘Yes,’ Jim agreed. ‘You might be right. It could certainly help us to refine housekeeping procedures.’ ‘Do you think that introducing selfmanaged teams in housekeeping would be the answer?’ Deborah asked. She had been doing some reading about this for a course. ‘It might make the staff talk and listen to each other a bit more.’ Jim was doubtful but prepared to be encouraging. ‘Perhaps,’ he said. ‘I don’t know much about it. Perhaps you could suggest it to Jade?’ Deborah was surprised. She had been thinking of just going ahead with a small trial. But on mature reflection, she realized that Jade’s support was probably essential for long-term success. Jade, it turned out, was prepared to support the introduction of self-managed teams, on condition that it was tried out first on a small number of rooms and no more than 20 altogether. As she left Jade’s office, Deborah thought to herself that she had been thinking of Jade as inflexible, but that wasn’t true. Jade had shown that she was open to new ideas, and prepared to consider incremental change at least sometimes.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Wk3 Knowledge Check | Sources of Resistance to Change: 1-) Which of the following is a common source of resistance to change in organizations? A) Clear communication B) Employee uncertainty and fear of the unknown C) Strong leadership D) Increased training opportunities  2-) How can organizational culture contribute to resistance to change? A) By fostering innovation and flexibility B) By reinforcing established routines and norms C) By encouraging continuous improvement D) By promoting open communication  Strategies for Managing Resistance: 3-) Which strategy is effective for managing resistance to change? A) Ignoring employee concerns B) Involving employees in the change process C) Mandating changes without explanation D) Reducing communication about the change  4-) Which of the following can help in overcoming resistance to change? A) Increasing workload without support B) Providing training and support during the transition C) Limiting feedback mechanisms D) Avoiding discussions about the change  Change Implementation Techniques: 5-) What is a key component of successful change implementation? A) Rigid adherence to old processes B) Flexible planning and adaptation C) Exclusion of employee feedback D) Maintaining the status quo  6-) Which technique is commonly used in change implementation? A) Gradual phased approach B) Sudden and unplanned changes C) Ignoring stakeholder input D) Avoiding pilot testing  Monitoring and Evaluation Skills: 7-) Why is monitoring and evaluation important in change management? A) To ensure that change initiatives are forgotten B) To track progress and make necessary adjustments C) To avoid documenting outcomes D) To halt the change process  8-) Which tool can be used for monitoring the progress of change initiatives? A) SWOT Analysis B) Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) C) Marketing Mix D) PEST Analysis  Sustaining Change: 9-) Which approach helps in sustaining change within an organization? A) Reverting to old habits B) Embedding new practices into organizational culture C) Ignoring success stories D) Avoiding follow-up actions  10-) What is crucial for sustaining change over the long term? A) Lack of leadership commitment B) Continuous reinforcement and support C) Resistance to new ideas D) Avoiding stakeholder engagement |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a future-proof strategy for a company operating in that industry, taking into account the drivers of digital transformation discussed in Week 1. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Present your strategy in the form of a written report, including a detailed implementation plan, and provide a justification for your strategic choices. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Assignment: Emerging Technologies Evaluation (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Explore the Gartner Hype Cycle and select three emerging technologies that are in different phases of the cycle (e.g., innovation trigger, peak of inflated expectations, plateau of productivity). |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and evaluate the potential applications, benefits, and challenges associated with each of the chosen technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create an infographic or visual presentation summarizing your findings and present it to the class, highlighting the technology's current stage and its implications for businesses. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 1 Project: Digital Transformation Roadmap (Estimated 10-12 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Imagine you are a consultant for a medium-sized company that is planning to embark on a digital transformation journey. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Develop a digital transformation roadmap that outlines the necessary steps and strategies for the company's successful digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| The roadmap should include an analysis of the company's current state, goals and objectives, recommended technologies, implementation plan, and potential challenges and mitigation strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Present your digital transformation roadmap in a professionally written report, including visual aids and supporting documentation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 7 - Week4:   | Understanding and Dealing with Change / Wk4: Enhancing Organizational Resilience and Future Trends in Change Management |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | In Module 7 you will be equipped with the essential competency of change management. You will learn about the principles, strategies, and tools of change management, helping you proficiently analyse the impact of change and discuss  comprehensive change management plans. You will gain understanding in identifying and addressing sources of resistance to change within organisations, necessary for facilitating smooth transitions. You will also learn to evaluate and select the most appropriate change management frameworks to guide organisational change efforts. Moreover, you will develop strategies to support organisational resilience in dynamic environments, ensuring that businesses can adapt and thrive in the face of change.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 7 Learning Outcomes | Wk1- Demonstrate understanding of change management principles, strategies, and tools to analyse the impact of change and develop comprehensive change management plans.  Wk2 - Evaluate and select appropriate change management frameworks and apply them to guide organisational change efforts.  Wk3 - Identify and address sources of resistance to change within organisations, leveraging effective strategies and communication. Wk4 - Develop strategies to enhance organisational resilience in dynamic environments. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Change management   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Workshop Outline | The 4 Core Change Principles and Future Organization  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 4 Project Learning Outcome | \- Develop strategies to enhance organisational resilience in dynamic environments. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Project | Strategic Change Management for the Future: Develop a comprehensive change management strategy for a hypothetical organization undergoing digital transformation, incorporating agile methodologies and addressing future trends. Details Below |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 PROJECT | Company: XYZ Corporation  Industry: Consumer Electronics  Situation: XYZ Corporation, a well-established player in the consumer electronics market, has thrived for decades by producing high-quality, innovative products. However, with rapid technological advancements and the shift towards smart, connected devices, XYZ faces fierce competition from more agile and tech-savvy companies like Apple and Samsung. This new landscape demands faster innovation cycles, enhanced customer experiences, and a more adaptive organizational structure.  Problem: XYZ Corporation's traditional hierarchical structure and centralized decision-making processes hinder its ability to quickly respond to market changes. The company has been slow to adopt new technologies and integrate customer feedback into product development. As a result, XYZ's market share and profitability have started to decline.  Learning Objectives: Understand the importance of evolving into an agile and adaptive entity. Apply as many principles as possible from 4 x Core principles of change management.  "Select Few - Diverse Many", "Have to -\> Want To", "Head & Heart", "Management & Leadership" Create a strategic change management plan to transform XYZ Corporation into a more dynamic and competitive organization.   Guidelines: Comprehensive Analysis: This assignment challenges you to integrate theoretical knowledge with practical application. It encourages a detailed analysis of agile methodologies, future trends, and strategic change management. Balanced View: Aim to present a balanced view that considers the potential benefits of agile methodologies and emerging trends, while addressing the challenges and risks of implementing change. Practical Recommendations: Your strategy should be underpinned by robust change management principles and include practical recommendations for real-world application.  Submission Instructions: Please submit your response as a PDF or Word document, approximately 500-700 words in length. Ensure your response includes all specified tasks and deliverables. Follow academic writing standards, providing clear explanations and rationale for your recommendations. Use APA style for citing sources and references.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | 1\.      Understanding of Agile Methodologies (20 points): •        Demonstrates thorough understanding of agile methodologies. •       Effectively explains how agile principles can be applied to change management. 2\.     Analysis of Future Trends (20 points): •       Identifies and discusses at least two emerging trends in change management. •       Analyzes the influence of these trends on future organizational change efforts. 3\.    Development of Change Management Strategies (20 points): •        Develops a comprehensive and strategic change management plan. •        Includes specific steps and actions for effective change management. 4\.     Addressing Challenges and Risks (20 points): •       Identifies potential challenges and risks associated with the strategy. •       Proposes practical solutions and risk mitigation measures. 5\.     Application of Strategic Thinking (10 points): •       Describes the application of strategic thinking and decision-making skills. •       Provides relevant examples of strategic decisions supporting the change process. 6\.     Practical Application (10 points): •       Applies the change management strategy to a real-world or hypothetical organization. •       Considers the unique context and challenges of the organization.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Knowledge Check | 1\.        What is the primary purpose of change management? A) To maintain the status quo B) To resist organizational change C) To manage and facilitate transitions within an organization D) To eliminate the need for organizational adaptation  2\.        Which of the following is a common source of resistance to change? A) Clear communication B) Employee empowerment C) Fear of the unknown D) Team collaboration  3\.        Which change management model emphasizes the importance of creating a sense of urgency and building a guiding coalition? A) Lewin's Change Management Model B) Kotter's 8-Step Process C) ADKAR Model D) Force Field Analysis  4\.        What is the purpose of a force field analysis in change management? A) To identify potential barriers and driving forces for change B) To determine the return on investment for change initiatives C) To select the most appropriate change management model D) To assess employee performance during change  5\.        Which leadership role is essential for driving and supporting change initiatives? A) Laissez-faire leader B) Transformational leader C) Transactional leader D) Authoritarian leader  6\.        What is a key characteristic of agile methodologies in change management? A) Linear and sequential project execution B) Rigidity and resistance to change C) Flexibility and adaptability to evolving requirements D) Centralized decision-making  7\.        How can organizations sustain change over the long term? A) By maintaining a rigid organizational structure B) By resisting future trends and innovations C) By embedding change into organizational culture D) By avoiding experimentation and risk-taking  8\.        What is the purpose of a change readiness assessment? A) To measure employee satisfaction B) To evaluate the effectiveness of change management models C) To assess the organization's readiness for change D) To determine the financial impact of change initiatives  9\.        Which factor is critical for successful change implementation? A) Maintaining the status quo B) Avoiding stakeholder involvement C) Clear communication and stakeholder engagement D) Rigid project plans and timelines  10\.        What is a primary benefit of adopting agile project management in change initiatives? A) Slower response to changing market conditions B) Linear and predictable project outcomes C) Enhanced collaboration and adaptability D) Strict adherence to predefined project plans  11\.         Which initiative did Procter & Gamble (P\&G) launch in 2008 to accelerate innovation? A) Innovate & Lead  B) Connect + Develop  C) Create & Conquer  D) Innovate + Accelerate  12\.         According to Kotter's "Few to Many" principle, what is crucial for uncovering leaders at all levels of an organization?  A) Relying solely on the top management  B) Encouraging only internal R\&D  C) Involving a diverse group of people D) Focusing on traditional leadership approaches  13\.         In the "Head + Heart" principle, what is emphasized to inspire people and achieve extraordinary results?  A) Strictly logical reasoning  B) The fundamental desire to contribute to something bigger than themselves  C) Solely rational understanding   D) Focus on individual performance 14\.         What did the general manager of a large manufacturing company realize about his third shift crew's engagement during a critical period? A) They preferred exhaustive emails  B) They responded well to informal, direct engagement C) They were unaffected by leadership communication   D) They resisted any form of change 15\.          What does the 21st century leader emphasize, according to the new leadership model? A) Exclusive top-level leadership  B) Strict hierarchical structures  C) Continuous learning, adaptability, and the ability to inspire changeD) Traditional views of management |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
