| MODULE 8:  | Agile Technology Leadership   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster the competency of Agile Technology Leadership. You will gain an understanding of contemporary leadership approaches within the technology domain, focusing on Servant Leadership principles. Throughout this module, you will be acquainted with collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies in a technology context, as part of the role of an Agile Leader. You will discuss Agile leadership principles to elevate collaboration, adaptability, and team performance, particularly within Agile teams and organisations engaged in technology projects or initiatives.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Agile Technology Leadership  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Demonstrate an understanding of modern approaches to effective leadership in the technology domain, with a specific focus on Servant Leadership principles. \- Apply collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies within a technology context as an Agile Leader. \- Utilise Agile leadership principles to enhance collaboration, adaptability, and team performance within technology projects or initiatives, emphasising Agile teams. \- Integrate Agile leadership practices across different organisational levels, demonstrating adaptability and promoting a culture of continuous improvement within technology teams and Agile organisations.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module 8 Week 1 Content  |  https://www.coursera.org/learn/agile-leadership-introduction-to-change?specialization=agile-leadership-change-management\#modules  https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/8uye4f6nr0qcpzl67dcx8/F1-Introduction-to-Agile-People-Principles.m4v?rlkey=f2wrqhq4fuom3a9t1zsqim7np\&e=1\&dl=0  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UZTyvbmW92M  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ctZHSa4Qhd4      |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Workshop Outline | •        Introduction to Agile Technology Leadership •        Importance of Leadership in Technology •        Agile and Servant Leadership Approaches in Technology |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment  | SCENARIO 5: ATTRACTING R\&D TALENT  Helen, Senior Vice President at BioFuture, a life sciences giant, faces a challenge. The company's R\&D activities are growing and becoming more geographically dispersed. However, traditional recruitment methods aren't attracting the young, skilled scientists they need in these new regions. Helen needs to convince regional HR teams and country general managers (focused on commercial and manufacturing) to adopt a new employer branding campaign and recruiting approach tailored to R\&D talent.  Your Task: Analyse the situation and recommend the most effective leadership approach for Helen to achieve her goals.  Key Considerations: The motivations and expectations of young R\&D talent differ from those in other company functions. They value: Stable, well-paid work Freedom to self-organize their work Interaction with the academic community Influence on R\&D direction Contribution to ethical research Career advancement in academia Regional HR teams need to understand the importance of the new approach and adapt it to local contexts. Country general managers, focused on commercial and manufacturing, need to be convinced of the value proposition for R\&D talent acquisition. Instructions: Analyze the leadership styles most suited to this situation (consider collaborative, visionary, and supportive styles). Explain how each leadership style can help Helen achieve success in gaining buy-in from regional HR and country general managers. Briefly discuss any potential challenges associated with each leadership style. Recommend the most effective leadership approach for Helen, considering the specific needs of each audience (regional HR vs. country general managers). Justify your recommendation by explaining how the chosen style will address the key considerations and achieve Helen's goals.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Knowledge Check | Question 1: What is Agile Technology Leadership? A. A traditional leadership style focusing on rigid hierarchies and clear chains of command. B. A leadership approach combining traditional styles with Agile principles, emphasizing flexibility, adaptability, and results. C. A leadership style that strictly follows autocratic decision-making processes. D. A passive leadership approach that allows team members to self-manage without any direction.  Question 2: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Agile Technology Leadership? A. Focus on Collaboration B. Empowerment and Self-Organization C. Strict adherence to predefined procedures D. Continuous Improvement  Question 3: Why is there an increasing need for Agile Leadership in the tech industry? A. Because it allows leaders to avoid making any changes. B. Due to the fast-paced and dynamic nature of technology, requiring innovation and quick adaptation. C. Because it focuses on maintaining the status quo. D. Due to its emphasis on rigid structures and processes.  Question 4: Which leadership style emphasizes building strong communication, empowerment, and delegation? A. Autocratic Leadership B. Servant Leadership C. Laissez-Faire Leadership D. Transformational Leadership  Question 5: What are some key components of Agile Technology Leadership? A. Rigid hierarchy and top-down decision making. B. Adaptability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. C. Centralized control and minimal team involvement. D. Isolating team members to work independently without feedback. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Clear understanding of different leadership styles and their characteristics. Well-reasoned analysis of how each style can benefit Helen. Critical assessment of potential challenges for each style. A well-supported recommendation for the most effective leadership approach. Strong justification based on the case specifics and Helen's goals. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 8:  | Agile Technology Leadership   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster the competency of Agile Technology Leadership. You will gain an understanding of contemporary leadership approaches within the technology domain, focusing on Servant Leadership principles. Throughout this module, you will be acquainted with collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies in a technology context, as part of the role of an Agile Leader. You will discuss Agile leadership principles to elevate collaboration, adaptability, and team performance, particularly within Agile teams and organisations engaged in technology projects or initiatives.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Agile Technology Leadership  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Demonstrate an understanding of modern approaches to effective leadership in the technology domain, with a specific focus on Servant Leadership principles. \- Apply collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies within a technology context as an Agile Leader. \- Utilise Agile leadership principles to enhance collaboration, adaptability, and team performance within technology projects or initiatives, emphasising Agile teams. \- Integrate Agile leadership practices across different organisational levels, demonstrating adaptability and promoting a culture of continuous improvement within technology teams and Agile organisations.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 2 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment  | Scenario: Acme Inc., a leading software development company, is transitioning from a waterfall development methodology to a more Agile approach. While the development team is enthusiastic about the change, the marketing department remains skeptical. The marketing team is concerned that the faster release cycles of Agile will disrupt their carefully planned marketing campaigns and lead to inconsistencies in messaging.  Your Task: As an Agile Leadership Consultant, you have been brought in to help bridge the gap between the development and marketing teams.  Instructions: Analyse the situation: Identify the key challenges Acme Inc. faces in implementing Agile across the organization. Develop an Agile Leadership Strategy: Recommend specific strategies Helen, the CEO, can use to create a collaborative environment where both development and marketing teams can thrive under the Agile umbrella. Consider incorporating elements of collaborative, coaching, and visionary leadership styles. Focus on strategies that address the marketing team's concerns and foster a shared understanding of the benefits of Agile. Implementation Plan: Briefly outline an implementation plan for your recommended leadership strategy. This plan might include communication methods, training initiatives, or team-building activities. Evaluation: Describe how you would measure the success of your proposed leadership strategy.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Knowledge Check | Question 1: Which of the following is NOT a core principle of Agile methodologies? A-Iterative development  B-Continuous improvement  C-Strict hierarchical leadership structure   D-Self-organizing teams  Question2: How does Agile leadership differ most from traditional leadership styles? A-Agile leaders focus more on individual performance metrics.  B-Agile leaders empower teams and encourage collaboration.  C-Agile leaders prioritize detailed planning for long-term projects.  D-Agile leaders avoid change and focus on maintaining the status quo.  Question3: What is the most important factor in building a successful Agile team? A-Implementing complex project management software.  B-Setting clear team goals that are not aligned with Agile principles.  C-Fostering trust, communication, and psychological safety within the team.  D-Assigning individual blame for team failures.  Question 4: How can Agile leaders encourage a culture of continuous improvement within their teams? A-Micromanaging team activities and deliverables.  B-Holding regular retrospectives to gather feedback and identify areas for improvement.  C-Avoiding any changes to the team's workflow, even if there are inefficiencies.  D-Prioritizing individual learning over team collaboration.  Question5: When setting goals for an Agile team, it's important to use the SMART framework. What does the "M" in SMART stand for? A-Mandatory  B-Measurable C-Motivational  D-Manageable |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Grading Rubric: Analysis of Challenges (20 points) Agile Leadership Strategy (40 points) \- Creativity and relevance to the case (20 points) \- Integration of different leadership styles (10 points) \- Addressing marketing team concerns (10 points) Implementation Plan (20 points) Evaluation Methods (20 points) Bonus: Briefly discuss any potential risks associated with your proposed leadership strategy and how you would mitigate them.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment: Future-Proof Strategy Development (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Choose an industry of your interest and conduct a strategic analysis of its competitive landscape in the context of digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 8:  | Agile Technology Leadership   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster the competency of Agile Technology Leadership. You will gain an understanding of contemporary leadership approaches within the technology domain, focusing on Servant Leadership principles. Throughout this module, you will be acquainted with collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies in a technology context, as part of the role of an Agile Leader. You will discuss Agile leadership principles to elevate collaboration, adaptability, and team performance, particularly within Agile teams and organisations engaged in technology projects or initiatives.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 3 Assignment  | Scenario: TechFusion, a leading technology company, is transitioning from a traditional waterfall development methodology to an Agile approach. The development team is eager to adopt Agile, but the customer support department is resistant, fearing that the iterative development cycles will lead to increased customer complaints and support workload.  Your Task: As an Agile Leadership Consultant, you have been hired to help integrate Agile practices across the development and customer support teams.  Instructions: 1-) Analyze the Situation: Identify the key challenges TechFusion faces in implementing Agile across the organization. Consider the concerns of both the development and customer support teams. 2-) Develop an Agile Leadership Strategy: Recommend specific strategies for Maria, the CEO, to create a collaborative environment where both development and customer support teams can thrive under Agile. Incorporate elements of collaborative, coaching, and visionary leadership styles. Focus on strategies that address the customer support team's concerns and foster a shared understanding of Agile's benefits. 3-) Implementation Plan: Briefly outline an implementation plan for your recommended leadership strategy. This plan might include communication methods, training initiatives, or team-building activities. Consider how to effectively communicate the changes and provide ongoing support. 4-) Evaluation: Describe how you would measure the success of your proposed leadership strategy. Identify key performance indicators (KPIs) and feedback mechanisms. 5-) Bonus: Risk Management: Briefly discuss any potential risks associated with your proposed leadership strategy and how you would mitigate them.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Knowledge Check | Question 1: What are the four core values of the Agile Manifesto? A- Customer collaboration, responding to change, following a plan, and comprehensive documentation B- Individuals and interactions, processes and tools, customer collaboration, and comprehensive documentation C- Individuals and interactions, working solutions, customer collaboration, and responding to change D- Customer collaboration, comprehensive documentation, following a plan, and responding to change  Question 2: Which Agile framework is best suited for development projects with well-defined scopes and timelines, involving small to medium-sized, cross-functional teams working in iterative sprints? A- Kanban B- Lean C- Scrum D- SAFe  Question 3: In the context of Agile leadership, what does it mean to "make it personal"? A- Leaders should make decisions based on personal preferences B- Change should be personally meaningful to employees, supporting them in understanding what an Agile mindset means to them C- Leaders should delegate all tasks to team members D- Leaders should focus on their own professional development  Question 4: What is a key advantage of the Kanban framework? A- It has a rigid structure with time-boxed iterations B- It allows for high flexibility and visual management of work in progress C- It focuses solely on product development D- It requires a cultural shift towards continuous improvement  Question 5: Which of the following is a responsibility of Agile leaders in fostering an Agile culture? A- Enforcing strict hierarchical structures B- Making unilateral decisions without team input C- Embedding Agile principles into the organization's structures, processes, and technology D- Avoiding any form of monitoring and learning        |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Grading Rubric: Analysis of Challenges (20 points) \- Clear identification of key challenges and concerns. \- Depth of analysis and understanding of the situation.   Agile Leadership Strategy (40 points) \- Creativity and relevance to the case (20 points) \- Integration of different leadership styles (10 points) \- Addressing customer support team concerns (10 points)  Implementation Plan (20 points) \- Practicality and feasibility of the plan. \- Inclusion of communication, training, and team-building strategies.  Evaluation Methods (20 points) \- Clear and measurable KPIs. \- Effective feedback mechanisms.  Bonus: Risk Management (10 points) \- Identification of potential risks. \- Proposed mitigation strategies.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 8:  | Agile Technology Leadership   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module aims to foster the competency of Agile Technology Leadership. You will gain an understanding of contemporary leadership approaches within the technology domain, focusing on Servant Leadership principles. Throughout this module, you will be acquainted with collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies in a technology context, as part of the role of an Agile Leader. You will discuss Agile leadership principles to elevate collaboration, adaptability, and team performance, particularly within Agile teams and organisations engaged in technology projects or initiatives.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Agile Technology Leadership  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Demonstrate an understanding of modern approaches to effective leadership in the technology domain, with a specific focus on Servant Leadership principles. \- Apply collaborative, adaptable, and results-driven leadership strategies within a technology context as an Agile Leader. \- Utilise Agile leadership principles to enhance collaboration, adaptability, and team performance within technology projects or initiatives, emphasising Agile teams. \- Integrate Agile leadership practices across different organisational levels, demonstrating adaptability and promoting a culture of continuous improvement within technology teams and Agile organisations.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 4 Assignment  | InnovateCorp, a global manufacturing company, is transitioning from a traditional hierarchical structure to an Agile organization. The engineering team is enthusiastic about Agile adoption, while the sales and marketing departments are apprehensive, fearing that the Agile approach will disrupt their well-established processes and increase their workload. Your Task: As an Agile Leadership Consultant, you have been hired to facilitate the integration of Agile practices across all departments at InnovateCorp. Instructions: Analyze the Situation: Identify the key challenges InnovateCorp faces in implementing Agile across the organization. Consider the concerns of both the engineering team and the sales and marketing departments. Develop an Agile Leadership Strategy: Recommend specific strategies for David, the CEO, to create a collaborative environment where all departments can thrive under Agile. Incorporate elements of collaborative, coaching, and visionary leadership styles. Focus on strategies that address the concerns of the sales and marketing departments and foster a shared understanding of Agile’s benefits. Implementation Plan: Briefly outline an implementation plan for your recommended leadership strategy. This plan might include communication methods, training initiatives, or team-building activities. Consider how to effectively communicate the changes and provide ongoing support. Evaluation: Describe how you would measure the success of your proposed leadership strategy. Identify key performance indicators (KPIs) and feedback mechanisms. Bonus: Risk Management: Briefly discuss any potential risks associated with your proposed leadership strategy and how you would mitigate them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Knowledge Check | Question 1: What is the primary objective of the Aspire, Design, Pilot stage in an Agile transformation? To implement Agile practices across all departments immediately To build the top team’s understanding and aspirations, create a blueprint, and learn through Agile pilots To focus solely on the development team’s adoption of Agile practices To measure the success of Agile practices after full implementation  Question 2: Which of the following is a key benefit of creating cross-functional teams during an Agile transformation? Increased bureaucracy and slower decision-making Enhanced collaboration and faster decision-making Greater control over individual team members Improved ability to maintain traditional hierarchies  Question 3: What approach did Spotify use to successfully implement Agile practices in their organization? Top-down command and control Centralized decision-making Squad model with autonomous teams and a flat hierarchy Maintaining traditional hierarchical structures  Question 4: In the context of an Agile organization, what does the term "backbone transformation" refer to? The physical redesign of office spaces The transformation of decision-making, resource allocation, and risk management processes The implementation of new software tools The creation of new marketing strategies  Question 5: Which company used a Sounding Board of 70 diverse volunteers to define the behavioural shifts needed for Agile culture transformation? Netflix Spark (New Zealand-based digital services company) ING Spotify   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 9:  | Aligning Agile Teams and Organisations through OKRs |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 9 aims to equip you with the crucial competency of managing businesses through Objectives and Key Results (OKRs). You will discuss how to define and interpret the concept of OKRs and their pivotal role in aligning organisational goals. You will also showcase a high-level understanding of implementing OKRs within an organisation, encompassing the skills necessary for setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. This module emphasises the significance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) within the OKR framework, enhancing your proficiency in nurturing a culture of growth. Lastly, you will illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its profound impact on goal achievement within organisations, preparing you to be adept at orchestrating successful business alignment through this strategic framework. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Managing business through OKRs  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Effectively define and explain the concept of Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and their significance in organisational goal alignment. \- Demonstrate a high level understanding in implementing OKRs within an organisation, including setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. \- Analyse the importance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) in the context of OKRs. \- Illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its impact on goal achievement within organisations.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 1 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment  | InnovateTech Inc., a growing tech company, is looking to implement Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) to enhance goal alignment and drive business performance. While the development and product teams are enthusiastic about adopting OKRs, the sales and marketing departments are sceptical. They are concerned that OKRs might disrupt their workflows and lead to unrealistic targets.  Your Task: Analyse the situation and recommend the most effective approach for Alex, the CEO, to explain and implement OKRs at InnovateTech Inc., focusing on their key benefits and strategic importance, as well as their structure and components.  Key Considerations: Different departments have varying motivations and concerns: Development and product teams value: Innovation and creativity Clear project priorities Regular feedback and iterative processes Sales and marketing teams value: Clear, measurable performance metrics Predictable targets Recognition and rewards based on performance Teams need to understand the significance of OKRs and how they contribute to overall organizational success. Leadership must address concerns and ensure a smooth transition without disrupting ongoing operations. Instructions: Analyse the Situation: Identify the key challenges InnovateTech Inc. faces in implementing OKRs across the organization. Explain the Key Benefits and Strategic Importance of OKRs: Discuss how OKRs help align organizational goals, drive performance, and enhance transparency and accountability. Highlight the specific benefits for both the organization and individual teams. Describe the Structure and Components of OKRs: Define Objectives and Key Results, and explain their characteristics. Provide examples of well-structured OKRs. Application and Justification: Recommend how Alex can communicate the key benefits and structure of OKRs to different departments. Justify how this approach will address the concerns of the sales and marketing departments and foster a shared understanding of OKRs. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Knowledge Check | Question 1: What do OKRs primarily attempt to address? A) Managing project timelines effectively B) Improving team collaboration C) Aligning organizational goals and measuring progress D) Enhancing employee motivation  Question 2: Which of the following is NOT typically an employee concern about OKR adoption? A) Fear of micromanagement B) Lack of clarity on company objectives C) Overemphasis on individual performance over teamwork D) Excessive focus on long-term goals  Question 3: Which statement best summarizes the difference between OKRs and KPIs? A) KPIs focus on measuring specific metrics, while OKRs emphasize setting ambitious objectives. B) OKRs are primarily used for individual performance evaluation, whereas KPIs assess overall organizational performance. C) KPIs are qualitative, while OKRs are quantitative in nature. D) OKRs measure outcomes achieved, while KPIs track ongoing performance metrics.  Question 4: Which of the following is a benefit of OKRs to employees and teams? A-) Improved salary packages B-) Clear and measurable performance metrics C-) Increased vacation days D-) Enhanced office amenities  Question 5: What are the two main components of OKRs? A-) Tasks and Milestones B-) Objectives and Key Results C-) Goals and Feedback D-) Strategies and Outcomes  Question 6: How often are OKRs typically evaluated? A-) Annually B-) Bi-annually C-) Quarterly D-) Monthly  Question 7: Which of the following statements best describes a powerful objective in OKRs? A-) It is task-oriented and detailed. B-) It is inspiring, qualitative, and aspirational. C-) It focuses on individual achievements. D-) It is vague and broad to cover multiple areas. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Evaluation Rubric  | Criteria to be used for scoring: Demonstrate a Deep Understanding of OKRs: Excellent score is 5 and it means: The student demonstrates a thorough understanding of the key benefits and strategic importance of OKRs, as well as their structure and components. Analysis of the Situation: Excellent score is 5 and it means: The analysis of challenges faced by InnovateTech Inc. in implementing OKRs is comprehensive and insightful. The student identifies all key challenges and demonstrates a deep knowledge of organizational dynamics. Explanation of Key Benefits and Strategic Importance: Excellent score is 5 and it means: The explanation of OKRs' benefits and strategic importance is clear, detailed, and well-supported by examples. Description of Structure and Components: Excellent score is 5 and it means: The description of the structure and components of OKRs is precise and includes relevant examples. The student demonstrates a strong grasp of how to formulate effective OKRs. Application and Justification: Excellent score is 5 and it means: The recommendation for communicating OKRs is well-reasoned and thoroughly justified. The student addresses all key considerations and provides a clear rationale for their approach. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 9:  | Aligning Agile Teams and Organisations through OKRs |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 9 aims to equip you with the crucial competency of managing businesses through Objectives and Key Results (OKRs). You will discuss how to define and interpret the concept of OKRs and their pivotal role in aligning organisational goals. You will also showcase a high-level understanding of implementing OKRs within an organisation, encompassing the skills necessary for setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. This module emphasises the significance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) within the OKR framework, enhancing your proficiency in nurturing a culture of growth. Lastly, you will illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its profound impact on goal achievement within organisations, preparing you to be adept at orchestrating successful business alignment through this strategic framework. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Managing business through OKRs  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Effectively define and explain the concept of Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and their significance in organisational goal alignment. \- Demonstrate a high level understanding in implementing OKRs within an organisation, including setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. \- Analyse the importance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) in the context of OKRs. \- Illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its impact on goal achievement within organisations.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 2 Assignment  | GreenEnergy Corp., a leading renewable energy solutions provider, aims to accelerate its growth and market leadership. The company has multiple divisions including solar, wind, and energy storage. While the executive team understands the potential of OKRs, there is resistance from middle management and operational teams who are concerned about added workload and potential disruption to existing processes.  Your Task: As a strategic consultant, develop an OKR implementation plan for GreenEnergy Corp. addressing the following: \- Analyze the Situation: Identify the key challenges and opportunities for OKR implementation. \- Develop an OKR Framework: Create a comprehensive OKR framework aligned with the company's vision and strategy. \- Address Departmental Concerns: Outline strategies to address the concerns of different departments and foster buy-in. \- Implementation Plan: Develop a step-by-step plan for rolling out OKRs across the organization. \- Measurement and Evaluation: Define metrics and KPIs to assess the effectiveness of the OKR implementation.  Key Considerations: \- Decentralized Structure: GreenEnergy Corp. has multiple divisions with varying levels of autonomy. \- Industry Dynamics: The renewable energy sector is highly competitive and subject to government policies and technological advancements. \- Cultural Shift: The company needs to foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and accountability. \- Data Availability: Ensuring access to relevant data for measuring key results is crucial.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Knowledge Check | Question 1: How do I know if I have defined the correct Key Results (KR)? A-) When It's Challenging B-) When understood by team members C-) When it is Challenging, Achievable and Measurable D-) Only when I get positive feedback  Question 2: What is the difference between Output and Outcome? A-) Both are the same B-) Tasks represent processes, Results represent the value we create C-) Tasks can be measured, results cannot D-) Results are defined as a list of tasks  Question 3: Who is responsible for Key Results (KR)? Can there be more than one person? A-) Usually one person is responsible, no more than one person B-) The whole team is responsible C-) Usually one person is the main person responsible, but more than one person can help D-) Only top management is responsible  Question 4: What happens to OKRs that I cannot reach in a quarter? A-) is ignored B-) carried over to the next quarter C-) Reviewed and redefined as necessary D-) Replaced immediately  Question 5: What are we doing wrong if we don't hit our OKRs? What could be the primary reason? A-) We don't work hard enough B-) Our KRs are not measurable C-) We don't have the right resources D-) Our goals are unrealistic or not well defined  Question 6: My Key Results (KR) are difficult to measure. Should I define a metric? A-) No, metrics are only required for goals B-) Yes, a specific metric must be defined for each KR C-) Only if KR is not measurable D-) Metrics are only necessary for large companies  Question 7: I completed all the Key Results (KR) but still the Goal (O) was not achieved, is it possible? A-) Yes, this could happen B-) No, this is impossible C-) Can happen if KRs are defined incorrectly D-) Can happen if goals are defined incorrectly  Question 8: How can I introduce OKRs to all employees in a company of 250 people at the same time? What is the best method? A-) By email B-) By organizing a group training session C-) By making individual meetings D-) By introducing it only to administrators  Question 9: How do I know if the Key Result (KR) is the KR and not the Goal (O)? A-) KRs are measurable, objectives (O) are more general and indicate what is intended to be achieved B-) KRs should be long term, goals (O) should be short term C-) KRs refer to processes, objectives (O) refer to results D-) Goals (O) can be measured, KRs should be general  Question 10: Is it necessary to define OKRs for routine and daily tasks? A-) Yes, OKRs should be defined for each task B-) No, OKR should focus on strategic objectives C-) Only for large projects D-) Only for annual goals    |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 9:  | Aligning Agile Teams and Organisations through OKRs |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 9 aims to equip you with the crucial competency of managing businesses through Objectives and Key Results (OKRs). You will discuss how to define and interpret the concept of OKRs and their pivotal role in aligning organisational goals. You will also showcase a high-level understanding of implementing OKRs within an organisation, encompassing the skills necessary for setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. This module emphasises the significance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) within the OKR framework, enhancing your proficiency in nurturing a culture of growth. Lastly, you will illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its profound impact on goal achievement within organisations, preparing you to be adept at orchestrating successful business alignment through this strategic framework. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Managing business through OKRs  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | \- Effectively define and explain the concept of Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and their significance in organisational goal alignment. \- Demonstrate a high level understanding in implementing OKRs within an organisation, including setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. \- Analyse the importance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) in the context of OKRs. \- Illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its impact on goal achievement within organisations.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 3 Assignment  | Potential OKR Mistakes and Challenges Scenario: EcoTech Solutions is a mid-sized company specializing in developing innovative technologies for sustainable agriculture. The company has recently decided to adopt the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) framework to drive alignment, focus, and performance across all its departments, including Research & Development, Sales, Marketing, and Operations. Despite the initial enthusiasm from the executive team, several challenges have emerged during the early stages of OKR implementation: \- Resistance to Change: Some team members are hesitant to embrace OKRs, fearing the disruption it may cause to their current workflows and responsibilities. \- Setting Unrealistic Goals: The Sales department has set overly ambitious OKRs, leading to stress and burnout among team members as they struggle to meet unattainable targets. \- Lack of Alignment: The Marketing department's OKRs are not fully aligned with the company's overall strategic objectives, causing confusion and misaligned efforts. \- Measurement and Evaluation Issues: The Operations team is struggling with defining clear metrics and key results, making it difficult to track progress effectively. \- Neglecting Regular Reviews: Teams are not consistently reviewing their OKRs, leading to missed opportunities for course correction and learning.  Your Task: As a strategic consultant, you have been hired by EcoTech Solutions to help them overcome these challenges and optimize their OKR implementation process. Your assignment includes the following tasks: \- Analyze the Situation: Identify the root causes of the challenges faced by each department. Consider the organizational culture, communication gaps, and the existing processes that may be contributing to these issues. \- Develop Solutions for Each Challenge: Propose innovative solutions to address the resistance to change, unrealistic goal setting, lack of alignment, measurement issues, and the neglect of regular OKR reviews. Provide specific examples of how these solutions can be implemented in EcoTech Solutions. \- Create a Revised OKR Framework: Based on your analysis and proposed solutions, design a revised OKR framework for EcoTech Solutions. Ensure that the new framework is aligned with the company’s strategic goals and addresses the challenges identified. \- Foster Departmental Buy-In: Outline strategies to engage and motivate each department to embrace the revised OKR framework. Include approaches to improve communication, collaboration, and accountability across teams. \- Implementation and Monitoring Plan: Develop a step-by-step plan for rolling out the revised OKR framework across the organization. Include key milestones, timelines, and responsibilities for monitoring progress and adjusting as needed. \- Evaluation Metrics: Define clear metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess the effectiveness of the new OKR implementation. Explain how these metrics will be used to drive continuous improvement and ensure the long-term success of OKRs at EcoTech Solutions.  Key Considerations: \- Cross-Departmental Alignment: Ensure that OKRs across departments are interconnected and contribute to the overall company objectives. Iterative Improvement: Promote a culture of continuous learning and iterative improvement, particularly in the areas of goal setting, progress tracking, and review. \- Employee Engagement: Focus on fostering a positive organizational culture where employees are motivated and supported in their pursuit of ambitious yet achievable goals. \- Data-Driven Decision Making: Emphasize the importance of using data and clear metrics to drive decision-making and evaluate progress.  Submit your detailed assignment report addressing each of the tasks above. Your report should demonstrate a deep understanding of OKR challenges and present practical solutions tailored to the specific needs of EcoTech Solutions.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Knowledge Check | Question 1: Which of the following is NOT a common mistake or challenge when implementing OKRs? A-) Resistance to change B-) Setting overambitious or unrealistic goals C-) Lack of alignment and clarity D-) Excessive communication among teams  Question 2: What innovative approach can be used to address the challenge of resistance to change during OKR implementation? A-) Implementing stricter deadlines B-) Fostering a culture of learning C-) Increasing workloads D-) Ignoring the concerns of early adopters  Question 3: Which of the following strategies helps to handle the challenge of setting overambitious or unrealistic goals in OKRs? A-) Encourage competition among teams B-) Use the "Goldilocks\*" principle C-) Minimize cross-functional collaboration D-) Avoid setting measurable key results  \*The "Goldilocks" principle in goal setting is about finding the right balance between ambition and achievability, ensuring goals are challenging but not unrealistic.  Question 4: What is a recommended solution for dealing with the lack of alignment and clarity in OKRs? A-) Reducing the frequency of team meetings B-) Visualizing alignment across departments C-) Limiting OKRs to executive levels only D-) Focusing solely on individual objectives  Question 5: What is one way to ensure continuous improvement in OKR performance according to the deck? A-) Applying more resources when needed B-) Setting OKRs only once per year C-) Avoiding regular progress tracking D-) Discouraging feedback from employees |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 9:  | Aligning Agile Teams and Organisations through OKRs |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | Module 9 aims to equip you with the crucial competency of managing businesses through Objectives and Key Results (OKRs). You will discuss how to define and interpret the concept of OKRs and their pivotal role in aligning organisational goals. You will also showcase a high-level understanding of implementing OKRs within an organisation, encompassing the skills necessary for setting, tracking, and evaluating objectives and key results. This module emphasises the significance of continuous improvement through CFRs (Conversations, Feedback, and Recognition) within the OKR framework, enhancing your proficiency in nurturing a culture of growth. Lastly, you will illustrate the iterative nature of the OKR life cycle and its profound impact on goal achievement within organisations, preparing you to be adept at orchestrating successful business alignment through this strategic framework. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Managing business through OKRs  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 4 Project Assignment  | Project Assignment: Crafting OKRs for Complex Organizational Challenges Assignment Title: Designing Effective OKRs for Strategic Transformation in a Global Organization  Introduction: In this project assignment, you are tasked with applying the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) framework to help a global organization overcome specific, complex challenges. Your objective is to develop OKRs that align different departments and teams around shared goals, drive accountability, and ensure measurable progress. The organization you are working with, GreenFuture, is a multinational company focused on environmental sustainability. Recently, the company has embarked on a major initiative to reduce its global carbon footprint, implement eco-friendly supply chain practices, and increase its market share in the green technology sector. This initiative involves multiple departments, including supply chain management, marketing, R\&D, and regional offices in different continents.  Task: You will act as an internal consultant, developing a robust OKR framework for GreenFuture to ensure successful execution of this complex initiative. Your project will include the following components: Define the Organizational Challenge: Select one of the company’s primary strategic challenges (e.g., reducing the carbon footprint across the supply chain, increasing customer adoption of green products, or improving employee engagement in sustainability practices). Describe the challenge in detail, explaining why it is critical for GreenFuture's overall success and how it involves multiple teams. Craft an Objective: Develop a clear, inspiring Objective (O) that addresses the organizational challenge. Ensure the Objective aligns with the company’s strategic vision and inspires cross-departmental collaboration. Design Key Results: Propose 3-4 measurable Key Results (KRs) for the Objective. These Key Results should be quantifiable, time-bound, and challenging but achievable. Ensure the Key Results can be tracked and assessed regularly to measure progress and impact. Align with Different Departments:  Explain how different departments (e.g., marketing, supply chain, regional offices, and R\&D) will contribute to the achievement of the OKRs. Discuss how you will ensure alignment between teams to drive cohesive efforts towards achieving the Objective. Overcoming Challenges: Identify potential challenges or barriers (e.g., resistance to change, lack of alignment, or data tracking issues) that may arise during OKR implementation. Propose solutions for overcoming these challenges to ensure OKRs are adopted smoothly and successfully across the organization. Evaluation and Feedback: Create a plan for regular evaluation of progress, feedback loops, and continuous improvement. Specify how managers and team leads will track progress and adjust OKRs as needed throughout the quarterly cycle. Guidelines: Your project should reflect a deep understanding of the OKR methodology, including how it fosters alignment, transparency, and performance. Ensure your proposed OKRs are realistic yet ambitious, pushing the organization towards significant impact. Consider the role of feedback and continuous improvement when implementing and adjusting OKRs in response to challenges.  Submission Instructions: Please submit your report as a PDF or Word document. The document should be 500-600 words in length. Focus on clarity, strategic alignment, and measurable outcomes. Learning Outcomes:  This assignment will deepen your understanding of how to design effective OKRs for complex projects and large-scale organizational change.  You will learn how to: Develop inspiring and actionable OKRs for cross-functional teams. Overcome barriers to OKR adoption. Drive continuous progress and improvement within an organization.  By applying these principles, you will gain practical insights into how OKRs can be used to transform business challenges into measurable, strategic outcomes.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4 Knowledge Check | 1\. What is one of the key benefits of using OKRs in management? A) They eliminate the need for regular progress reviews. B) They promote accountability and transparency across teams. C) They are only applicable to small teams with limited objectives. D) They remove the need for collaboration between departments.  2\. How do OKRs help with risk management? A) By eliminating the possibility of unforeseen risks. B) By promoting a reactive approach to risks. C) By providing real-time tracking and prioritization of risks based on their potential impact. D) By focusing solely on financial risks within the organization.  3\. Which of the following is an example of a Key Result for improving operational efficiency? A) Achieve a 20% reduction in product delivery times within Q2. B) Create a new product by Q4. C) Increase the company's market share in Europe. D) Set up monthly employee feedback meetings.  4\. Which of the following is a common challenge faced when implementing OKRs? A) Lack of executive involvement. B) Over-communication between teams. C) Setting goals that are too easy to achieve. D) Requiring too much alignment between departments.  5\. What is the primary purpose of setting OKRs in an organization? A) To ensure that every individual works independently on their own objectives. B) To align the organization around common goals and drive performance towards measurable outcomes. C) To focus on individual performance metrics unrelated to the organization’s strategic priorities. D) To provide yearly performance reviews.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 10:  | Agile Product Management  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module is designed to develop your expertise in Agile Project Management. You will gain a thorough understanding of Agile principles and cultivate an Agile mindset within the project management process, empowering you to manage projects more flexibly and effectively. This module will guide you in designing Agile project plans that align with organizational objectives and adapt to changing project requirements. Additionally, you will learn how to implement Agile methodologies for managing projects iteratively, integrating stakeholder feedback to enhance project outcomes. The module emphasizes the execution of project sprints using Agile techniques, fostering continuous improvement in project delivery and equipping you with the skills necessary to succeed in the fast-paced world of Agile Project Management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Agile Project Management & Product Development  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | Apply Agile principles and an Agile mindset to the project management process. Design an Agile project plan that aligns with organizational goals and adapts to changing project requirements. Implement Agile methodologies to manage projects iteratively, incorporating stakeholder feedback effectively. | Week 1 Assignment  | Objective/Focus: Develop a 1-page proposal to implement Agile Project Management to solve a common challenge in a traditional Waterfall project setup.  Learning Outcome: Understand the key differences between Agile and Waterfall project management and apply Agile Project Management to overcome project management challenges.  Instructions: You are a project manager at a company that traditionally uses the Waterfall approach. Due to recent challenges with project delays and inflexibility, top management is considering transitioning a new software development project to Agile.  Identify a common challenge faced in the current Waterfall approach (e.g., long planning cycles, scope creep, late testing). Propose how Agile project management  (e.g., iterative development, continuous feedback, flexibility) can solve this challenge. Highlight the expected benefits of transitioning from Waterfall to Agile (e.g., faster feedback loops, better customer satisfaction). Guidelines:  Submit a 1-page document in PDF format. Use Arial font, size 11, with single-line spacing. You may use course materials and external resources to support your argument. Resources:  Week 1 workshop slides. Recommended readings on Agile vs. Waterfall project management.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Knowledge Check | Question 1: What is a key advantage of Agile Project Management compared to Waterfall Project Management? Fixed scope and deliverables from the start Flexibility and adaptability Long-term planning with no need for iteration Hierarchical structure and control.  Question 2: The main constraints in a traditional / waterfall project life cycle are scope, cost and ? Risk. Communications. Quality Resources.   Question 3: Does Traditional/Waterfall Project Man welcome change and take advantage of change? YES NO SOME NOT AVAILABLE.  Question 4: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) in Agile? It is the simplest version of an idea that solves the core problem It gathers feedback from users early in the process It includes all the final features of the product It allows for iterative improvements based on feedback.  Question 5: What is a common risk in traditional Waterfall Project Management? Frequent customer feedback during all stages Potential scope creep due to ongoing changes Inflexibility to accommodate changes once the project has started Continuous improvement during the project lifecycle  Question 6: According to Agile principles, what is the best approach to reduce the cost of failure in a project? Detailed upfront planning and documentation Frequent testing and feedback at every stage of the project Waiting until the end to present the final product Avoiding any customer involvement until the project is complete  Question 7: In Agile, what is the main role of sprints? To complete a project in one big release To focus on long-term planning with no interruptions To deliver working functionality at regular intervals To eliminate feedback loops entirely   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining case studies and real-world examples of organizations that have successfully embraced digital transformation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Assessing the potential risks and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation and strategies for mitigating them. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Investigating the building blocks of a digital organization, including agile structures, data-driven decision-making, and digital talent management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Introducing the Digital Feedback Loop as a central framework for continuous improvement and innovation. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Reviewing the frameworks such as Gartner's Hype Cycle to identify the most relevant technologies and their potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 1 Assignment: Drivers of Digital Transformation Analysis (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Research and analyze three case studies of organizations that have undergone successful digital transformations (or Select one from the pool provided) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Identify and discuss the key drivers that led these organizations to embark on their digital transformation journeys. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a written report highlighting the commonalities and lessons learned from these case studies, and provide recommendations for other organizations seeking to initiate their own digital transformations. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment: Technology Disruption and Impact (Estimated 8 hours) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Select two emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented reality) and research their disruptive potential and impact on various industries. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prepare a comparative analysis of the two technologies, evaluating their benefits, challenges, and potential applications in business. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Create a visually engaging presentation summarizing your findings, and deliver a short presentation to the class on the disruptive nature of these technologies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 10:  | Agile Product Management  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module is designed to develop your expertise in Agile Project Management. You will gain a thorough understanding of Agile principles and cultivate an Agile mindset within the project management process, empowering you to manage projects more flexibly and effectively. This module will guide you in designing Agile project plans that align with organizational objectives and adapt to changing project requirements. Additionally, you will learn how to implement Agile methodologies for managing projects iteratively, integrating stakeholder feedback to enhance project outcomes. The module emphasizes the execution of project sprints using Agile techniques, fostering continuous improvement in project delivery and equipping you with the skills necessary to succeed in the fast-paced world of Agile Project Management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Agile Project Management & Product Development  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | Apply Agile principles and an Agile mindset to the project management process. Design an Agile project plan that aligns with organizational goals and adapts to changing project requirements. Implement Agile methodologies to manage projects iteratively, incorporating stakeholder feedback effectively. Execute project sprints using Agile techniques, emphasizing continuous improvement in project management processes.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 2 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2 Assignment  | Objective: Develop a compelling product vision and roadmap for a new mobile app, the Smart Travel Assistant App, designed to help travelers manage all aspects of their journey. The app is aimed at three key personas: Alex, Fatima, and Marcus, each with distinct needs and lifestyles.  Personas: Alex, The Adventurous Solo Traveler Age: 30 Occupation: Freelance photographer Location: Barcelona, Spain Personality: Curious, loves spontaneity and exploring new cultures Lifestyle: Often traveling to remote and off-the-beaten-path locations for photography projects Challenges/Needs: Alex needs a travel app that helps him with last-minute bookings, tracking expenses on the go, and finding unique local experiences. He prefers apps that work offline since he often travels to places with limited connectivity.  Fatima, The Organized Family Traveler Age: 42 Occupation: High school teacher Location: Dubai, UAE Personality: Highly organized, family-oriented Lifestyle: Travels with her family (husband and two kids) for holidays, usually planning several months in advance. She values detailed itineraries, budget control, and child-friendly travel suggestions. Challenges/Needs: Fatima needs a travel app that can help her organize all her travel logistics, find family-friendly accommodations, manage expenses, and suggest kid-friendly activities.  Marcus, The Efficiency-Driven Business Traveler Age: 38 Occupation: Sales Director at a multinational company Location: New York City, USA Personality: Time-conscious, values efficiency and productivity Lifestyle: Travels frequently for work, often on tight schedules. He needs to stay connected during travel and values premium services like fast-track at airports and high-speed internet for working on the go. Challenges/Needs: Marcus needs a travel app that integrates seamlessly with his work schedule, offers fast accommodation booking, helps him organize meetings, and offers productivity tools while traveling.  Assignment Guidelines:  Persona Analysis (1-2 paragraphs): Summarize the key needs and challenges of each persona (Alex, Fatima, and Marcus). Describe how each persona’s needs influence your product vision and feature prioritization.  Product Vision Statement (1 paragraph): Draft a vision statement for the Smart Travel Assistant App, considering how the product will address the needs of all three personas. Ensure the vision statement outlines the product’s goals, differentiation, and alignment with business strategy.  Feature Prioritization (Table or List): Using the list of product features provided in class (such as expense tracker, eco-friendly travel options, and productivity mode), prioritize these features based on business value and simplicity. Justify your prioritization by explaining which features are most important for each persona and how they align with the product’s vision.  Product Roadmap (1-page visual representation or table): Develop a high-level product roadmap that outlines the key milestones for feature releases. Consider external constraints, technical dependencies, and business objectives while planning feature rollouts over time.  Addressing Stakeholder Concerns (1 paragraph): Discuss potential challenges you might face from stakeholders (e.g., marketing, sales, or customer support) when implementing the product vision. Propose strategies for obtaining stakeholder buy-in and ensuring smooth product development.  Deliverables: 1-page Product Vision Statement and Persona Analysis 1-page Feature Prioritization Table 1-page Product Roadmap Visual 1-paragraph Stakeholder Concern Response  Learning Outcomes: Understand the importance of personas in shaping product vision and development. Learn how to prioritize product features using business value and simplicity as criteria. Gain experience in developing a product roadmap and aligning it with stakeholder expectations.   |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

A) To identify technical challenges in the product roadmap B) To create a fictional representation of the ideal customer based on research C) To ensure all stakeholders approve the product design D) To determine the final cost of product features  2\. According to the Agile methodology, why is it important to prioritize features based on business value and simplicity?  A) It reduces the need for sprint planning B) It speeds up the creation of personas C) It helps teams focus on delivering high-impact, easily implementable features first D) It simplifies the creation of technical backlogs  3\. Which of the following is a key component of a compelling product vision in Agile product development?  A) Detailed user interface mockups B) The company’s quarterly sales forecast C) A description of how the product meets customer needs and supports the company’s strategy D) A list of technical requirements for the development team  4\. In Agile product development, what does a “product backlog” consist of?  A) A list of technical debt items that need to be resolved B) A comprehensive list of all the user stories known for the product C) A breakdown of budgetary constraints for product development D) A series of product mockups  5\. What is the purpose of “release planning” in Agile product development?  A) To create a product roadmap for the next 5 years B) To define the release goal, target date, and prioritize backlog items C) To estimate the total cost of the product development D) To create wireframes and mockups for the product |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| MODULE 10:  | Agile Product Management  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module overview: | This module is designed to develop your expertise in Agile Project Management. You will gain a thorough understanding of Agile principles and cultivate an Agile mindset within the project management process, empowering you to manage projects more flexibly and effectively. This module will guide you in designing Agile project plans that align with organizational objectives and adapt to changing project requirements. Additionally, you will learn how to implement Agile methodologies for managing projects iteratively, integrating stakeholder feedback to enhance project outcomes. The module emphasizes the execution of project sprints using Agile techniques, fostering continuous improvement in project delivery and equipping you with the skills necessary to succeed in the fast-paced world of Agile Project Management. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Target Competency | Agile Product Management & Product Development  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Module Learning Outcomes  | Apply Agile principles and an Agile mindset to the project management process. Design an Agile project plan that aligns with organizational goals and adapts to changing project requirements. Implement Agile methodologies to manage projects iteratively, incorporating stakeholder feedback effectively. Execute project sprints using Agile techniques, emphasizing continuous improvement in project management processes.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| \[merged\] Week 3 Workshop Outline |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Assignment  | Objective/Focus: Develop a 1-page proposal outlining how Sprint Planning and Daily Scrum can be applied to solve inefficiencies in team collaboration and project progress tracking within a traditional Waterfall project.  Learning Outcome: Understand the role of Sprint Planning and Daily Scrum in Agile project management and demonstrate how these practices can improve team collaboration, project visibility, and adaptability.  Instructions: You are a project manager at a company that uses the Waterfall approach for product development. Your team struggles with poor communication, missed deadlines, and a lack of clear progress tracking. Management is open to adopting Agile practices to overcome these challenges. 1-) Identify a challenge your team currently faces in the Waterfall setup (e.g., poor communication between team members, lack of visibility into progress, or unclear task ownership). 2-) Propose how Sprint Planning and Daily Scrum can address this challenge: \- Explain how Sprint Planning can improve project structure, task ownership, and alignment with project goals. \- Highlight how Daily Scrum meetings can increase transparency, accountability, and team coordination. 3-) Highlight the expected benefits of incorporating Sprint Planning and Daily Scrum into your project management approach (e.g., better progress tracking, improved team communication, faster issue resolution).  Guidelines:  Submit a 1-page document in PDF format. Use Arial font, size 11, with single-line spacing. Use real-world examples where appropriate to make your argument. You may refer to course materials or external resources to support your proposal.  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3 Knowledge Check | 1-) What is the primary objective of Sprint Planning? A) To review completed user stories. B) To plan the overall project timeline. B) Roadblocks that the team is facing. C) Effort estimates for upcoming sprints. D) Progress made the previous day.  3-) What is the recommended duration of a Daily Scrum? A) Burnup chart B) Gantt chart C) Burndown chart D) Project charter   5-) What is the role of the Scrum Master during a Daily Scrum? A) To assign tasks to the team members. | Week 1: Introduction to Digital Transformation and its Drivers |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the concept of digital transformation and its significance in today's business landscape. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring the key drivers of digital transformation, such as technological advancements, changing customer expectations, and competitive pressures. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 2: Technology as an Agitator and Enabler |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Analyzing the role of technology as both an agitator and enabler in driving digital transformation initiatives. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring how emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and Internet of Things, are disrupting industries and transforming business models. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 3: Competitive Positioning and Future-Proof Strategies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Understanding the importance of competitive positioning in the digital age and how it differs from traditional business strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Exploring frameworks and methodologies for identifying competitive advantages and developing future-proof strategies. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Examining successful case studies of organizations that have effectively positioned themselves in the digital marketplace. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Week 4: Building Digital Organizations and Emerging Technologies |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
